items.body: This release is essentially a concept piece comprising a substantial 120-page book and an accompanying Soundtrack. Merciful Nuns needs no introduction by now, and their driving force, Artaud Seth, has found the perfect vehicle here to further flesh out his “Kvltan” universe. The book serves as a guide to the ancient civilization known as Kvltan, which predates known human civilization by a vast margin. It suggests that humanity’s origins lie much further back in space and time than we realize. It is a mythological narrative in which ancient gods, lost knowledge and rituals, portals to other dimensions, dream worlds, and much more converge. Central to this are the ‘Oneironauts’—individuals capable of entering other realms of consciousness through their dreams. The book constantly straddles the boundary between dream and reality, life and death, past and future. It acts as a narrative guide to which Merciful Nuns have composed the accompanying music. The release features a 33-minute-and-33-second track divided into four parts, followed by a second track. The first piece is particularly intriguing, sounding like a genuine film score—a departure from the German band’s usual style. It is entirely Cinematic in nature, defined by an omnipresent ritualistic atmosphere that gradually evolves. Spoken-word elements are incorporated alongside deep, rumbling vocals, while the use of strings further reinforces the Soundtrack aesthetic. To my ears, this piece complements the book perfectly. The second track feels more familiar, offering a blend of Metal guitar and Gothic atmosphere, topped off by Artaud Seth’s deep, charismatic vocals. Beyond the power of the guitars, the track is further enriched by piano passages. Fans of Merciful Nuns may find themselves faced with a somewhat atypical work here, but it fits perfectly within the band’s ritualistic dynamic. Moreover, the book itself is a relatively quick read, making the entire release an intriguing and immersive experience for anyone willing to step into the mysterious world of Kvltan. (Rating:7½). Watch the clip for “Black Monoliths”: About Merciful Nuns Merciful Nuns is the vehicle of German multi-instrumentalist Artaud Seth, formed in 2010 after the disbandment of his earlier band The Garden Of Delight. Seth also records as Near Earth Orbit and runs the Solar Lodge label, through which Merciful Nuns’ own catalogue is released. The project’s 2010 debut album, “Lib. I”, drew heavily on The Sisters Of Mercy; by 2022 Seth counted “Kvltan” as the band’s eleventh album, a fusion of industrial, gothic and psychedelic elements built around the mythology of the ancient civilisation Kvltan, as he explained in a Side-Line interview. “Liber Kvltanae” continues that story and the “Liber” naming convention set by the band’s debut.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是概念作品，配套一本120页的书籍与原声带，讲述名为Kvltan的史前文明神话叙事。核心概念围绕'梦行者'展开，探讨梦境与现实、生死、维度穿越等主题。首支曲目长达33分33秒，分为四个乐章，具有电影配乐质感，融合低沉的念白、嗡鸣人声与弦乐，营造仪式化的氛围。第二首曲目回归乐队熟悉的哥特暗潮路线，加入金属吉他与钢琴段落。整体音乐服务于书籍叙事，将哥特工业的黑暗美学与电影化配乐结合，为听众构建一个可供沉浸的异世界。Solar Lodge是该乐队主理人自己的独立厂牌，适合喜欢黑暗仪式感与跨媒介叙事的听众。

items.body:
After the OĽUN album I reviewed enthusiastically a while back, here’s the next project, again motivated and led by violinist/fiddler/composer Ján Kružliak Jr., continuing the rapprochement, indeed embrace, between Slovakia’s traditional music and its classical music. This time it reconnects the works of classical composers who were inspired by and drew on village musics with those traditional sources and styles.
Three ensembles are involved: the Spectrum Quartett led by Kru�liak with two violins, viola and cello; Nogaband, the traditional-style quartet of fiddles, contra (chording viola) and bass that’s led by fiddler and singer Michal Noga; and the female vocal group Ulijanky, plus guest singer Simona Hulejov�.
The majority of the tracks are interpretations of works by Slovak composer Eugen Suchon (1908-1993), with others from fellow-Slovaks Ilja Zeljenka (1932-2007) and Alexander Moyzes (1906-1984), and Hungarian B�la Bart�k (1881-1945) who did a lot of his very detailed collecting of folk music in Slovakia.
In each case the sources - musicians and locations in villages across Slovakia - are credited in the notes, and these arrangements and performances reconnect with the energy and traditional vocal sound of those sources.
In no way is this an orchestra-smoothed thing; this is gutsy, brilliantly played and sung music with all the spirit, skill and technique of traditional music, from players and singers who deeply understand and inhabit it. It’s a glorious piece of work, music to luxuriate in. There’s too much richness to begin to detail, but here’s a dip into a few moments to give the flavor. The tracks all have very long titles detailing their sources, so for brevity’s sake I’ll just give track numbers.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由小提琴家兼作曲家Ján Kružliak Jr.主导，旨在重新连接斯洛伐克传统民间音乐与受其启发的古典音乐作品。Spectrum Quartett弦乐四重奏、Nogaband传统弦乐组合与Ulijanky女声合唱团三方协作，曲目主要改编自斯洛伐克作曲家Eugen Suchon、Ilja Zeljenka、Alexander Moyzes以及曾深入斯洛伐克采录民间音乐的匈牙利作曲家巴托克。每首作品都在唱片内页中标注了采集自斯洛伐克各村镇的原始音乐来源与演奏者。演绎方式保留了民间音乐粗犷有力的能量与传统声乐音色，弦乐与声乐相互交织，将古典作曲技法与乡土根源质感熔为一炉。这种跨越民间与学院、传统与现代边界的融合思路，为听众提供了重新理解中东欧音乐传统的独特路径。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.
Find out more about Merodefestival.
Further reading and listening

(Interview)

Songbooks Live
(Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了十三支比利时创新乐团的作品，以鲁汶郊外1129年建立的帕克修道院为创作与录制核心。乐手们借助修道院的宁静氛围，将比利时民间传统与多种世界音乐元素相融合，包括罗姆人音阶、bal-musette手风琴风格、地中海与阿拉伯声响、匈牙利Citer琴等。作品中手风琴与西古典传统尤为突出，部分曲目带有巴洛克气质，另一些则涉及喉音唱法与爵士即兴。专辑历经三年制作，由Bert Huysentruyt录制混音，Pieter De Wagter母带处理，巧妙利用修道院古老石质空间带来的自然混响。整体风格跨度宽广却因共同的灵感来源而保持内在连贯，呈现温暖且令人惊喜的听觉体验。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑聚焦于俄罗斯将被占领区约两万乌克兰儿童强制送往俄境、企图改造其民族认同的战争罪行，以乌克兰传统歌谣与原创作品共同回应这一现实。音乐以弓弦乐器为主，辅以班杜拉琴与钢琴，加拿大与乌克兰两组音乐家远程协作完成。乌克兰乐组中包含一位曾亲身经历被掳、来自马里乌波尔的年轻乐手，她在双陶笛上贡献独奏段落。歌词层面既有对传统民歌的重新编排，将历史中被迫外出做工的少女命运与当下被劫掠的儿童处境并置，也有以乌克兰民间传说中河神、水妖等自然精灵为意象的祭祀歌曲，在温柔吟唱与激烈嘶喊之间切换情绪。专辑由乌加联合的Marichka与班杜拉琴手Alina Kuzma共同领衔，后者在加拿大组建全女性演出团体持续巡演。整张作品将地方民俗声乐传统置于当代人道议题之下，使音乐本身成为一种见证。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑汇集了圣多美和普林西比这一非洲第二小国在1970至80年代录制的Puxa舞曲。Puxa是一种融合多种元素的复合音乐，吸收了来自前葡萄牙非洲殖民地及加勒比海地区的merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等节奏与律动。该音乐文化背景独特，曾被殖民当局禁止但未能被压制。专辑展示了Pedro Lima领衔的乐队等艺术家的创作，以多把吉他交织缠绕的方式构建旋律框架，人声与器乐在groove上交替推进，体现出非洲岛屿特有的音乐语言。乐评通过地理与历史背景的补充，揭示了这些录音为何如此珍贵——它们来自一个录音工业极为有限的群岛，却保留了丰富的音乐创造力。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是挪威Camilla Hole Trio继上张融入科幻合成器元素的作品之后，以更为回归传统的方式对挪威西部民间舞曲音乐进行再创作。主奏乐器为高音萨克斯，融合了爵士乐即兴手法与北欧民间旋律素材。乐评以开篇曲为例详细分析了乐队的互动方式：三人角色不固定，主旋律在萨克斯与低音提琴之间流转，打击乐手以颤音琴拓展节奏空间，模块合成器的叠加为传统曲调增添色彩层次。整体呈现出即兴与传统、地方性与爵士语汇之间的跨界对话。对偏爱实验爵士与世界音乐融合的听众来说，这张专辑展现了斯堪的纳维亚音乐传统与前卫即兴思维结合的可能性。

as part of the
Prism Quartet
's new series of collaborations called

. If you have listened to my radio programs, you are probably familiar with the quartet's ground-breaking, genre-blurring music. If not, there's no better introduction than this.

items._cn_summary: 这张作品由作曲家大卫·祖宾斯基为普瑞姆萨克斯四重奏的「解锁你的内在作曲家」企划而创作，2025年11月在费城自由图书馆首演。演出邀请了诗人兼人声表演者厄休拉·拉克、打击乐手泰肖恩·索雷与小提琴家卡洛斯·圣地亚哥共同参与编创与演绎。全曲时长不到四分钟，经历了从原始粗粝到抒情柔美再回归的完整弧线，展现了室内乐编制与人声即兴之间的对话可能。编者在推荐中强调四重奏一贯的跨界与流派融合特质，将此曲视为该团体的代表性新作。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组合 GuldGanger 的首张数字 EP，共五部作品。乐队由北欧民谣圈资深歌手 Mia Guldhammer 领衔，乐手各自为传统曲目贡献不同诠释。开场曲以粗粝的律动展现主唱嗓音的说服力，铿锵的口簧与风笛为唯一原创曲注入持续推力。扬琴为传统民谣铺设精致底色，口簧的柔软吹奏在终曲中与笛子、弦乐交织，形成跳动而略显失衡的器乐张力。整体弥漫着古老而略带粗粝的氛围，五部作品已展现出超越新人阶段的成熟度，乐评期待他们未来完整专辑的展开。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴手Mats Edén与两位挪威演奏家组成三重奏，以非传统方式重新诠释斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲素材。Tellef Kvifte主奏高音竖笛并辅以萨克斯与风笛，其子Knut Kvifte Nesheim担任鼓手与作曲，三人皆致力于模糊不同音乐类型的界限。整体呈现更接近室内乐式的亲密对话而非舞蹈伴奏音乐，将民间舞曲中潜在的阴暗底色与神秘氛围挖掘出来。选曲涵盖挪威Setesdal山谷的小提琴曲与瑞典Polska等，演奏中旋律片段不断解体与重组，音乐发展充满即兴式的碎片化探索，展现了北欧民间音乐传统在实验性诠释下的隐藏维度。

items.album: “A trip through the other side of enlightenment”: Funkadelic reviewed
items.excerpt: Two newly reissued albums showcase the seismic psychedelia of George Clinton’s Funkadelic at its rawest and most disruptive, writes John Morrison in The Wire 512 Funkadelic Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Maggot Brain Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Released the summer before Jimi Hendrix tragically passed away in 1970, Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow was not only the follow-up to Funkadelic’s promising self-titled debut of the same year;
items.body: Two newly reissued albums showcase the seismic psychedelia of George Clinton’s Funkadelic at its rawest and most disruptive, writes John Morrison in The Wire 512 Funkadelic Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Maggot Brain Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Released the summer before Jimi Hendrix tragically passed away in 1970, Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow was not only the follow-up to Funkadelic’s promising self-titled debut of the same year; it signalled the arrival of George Clinton’s ensemble as the next great voice in Black rock and psychedelia. In his 2014 memoir Brothas Be, Yo Like George, Ain’t That Funkin’ Kinda Hard On You?, Clinton acknowledges this by contrasting the album’s release with Hendrix’s death, an event that he notes as “the end of an era”. During his brief but electrifying career, Hendrix moulded multiple aspects of the Black musical tradition – blues, rock, funk, R&B, jazz – into an electrifying corpus that opened up a new world of possibilities. With Hendrix dead and the psychedelic road map that he laid out for any adventurous soul to follow, Funkadelic went on to emerge as his mightiest descendents. While Funkadelic were recording Free Your Mind Clinton absorbed and pulled inspiration from underground comics, Black power/radical leftist theory and Erich von Däniken’s work theorising that aliens had made contact with and shaped the development of ancient human civilisations. Clinton took all the disparate cultural, historical, political and extraterrestrial influences swirling around in his head and drenched them in acid. The famously LSD soaked sessions produced an album that distilled the political, cultural and philosophical DNA of the 1960s into a new musical vision for the 70s. Built around Eddie Hazel’s gnarly blues and wah-wah drenched guitar, “Funky Dollar Bill” highlights the flipside of the concept of money as freedom explored on “Friday Night, August 14th”. With lyrics like "The pusher push, the fixer fix, the judge acquits, the junkie leads his life, for the dollar bill”, it's clear that here, money is less a vehicle for freedom than a tool for control. “Eulogy And Light” serves as the perfect album closer, with Clinton praying for strength in the face of temptation and moral degradation. In an innovative display of the band's willingness to experiment with sound and concepts, the music for “Eulogy And Light” is an earlier Funkadelic track called “Open Your Eyes” spun backwards. In doing this, Clinton and crew extract the source song's optimistic heart and repurpose its gospel-inspired tune into something stranger, more twisted. Free Your Mind opens with the epic ten minute title track. Amid a ghostly mass of distorted guitar, feedback and cosmic synthesizer bleeps, Clinton screams “Free your mind and your ass will follow/The kingdom of heaven is within!”. These simple yet spine-tingling chants formed something close to a succinct mission statement. More than just slogans, Clinton was directly addressing the intellectual, physical and spiritual demands of a new musical and ideological path. He has described “Friday Night, August 14th” as a “paycheck and party song” about how a little bit of money can buy a moment of joy and freedom. In that sense, the song feels like the spiritual heir to Louis Jordan's 1949 proto-rock ’n’ roll smash “Saturday Night Fish Fry”. By the time Funkadelic entered the United Sound Systems studio in Detroit to record the follow-up to Free Your Mind, the band were at once a formidable live unit and boundless experimenters in the studio. The result of those USS sessions was 1971’s Maggot Brain, one of the greatest psychedelic rock albums ever made and the crown jewel of Clinton’s extensive body of work. The album opens with a simple and ominous message that is both a continuation of the core theme examined throughout Free Your Mind and a harbinger of the band’s future: “I have tasted the maggots in the mind of the universe/I was not offended/For I knew I had to rise above it all/Or drown in my own shit”. Here the “maggots” are the corrosive forces of ignorance, self-doubt and control that infested Free Your Mind. To all intents and purposes, Maggot Brain is a trip through the other side of enlightenment, witnessed through the prism of life, death and the liberatory potential of madness. Famously, Clinton prompted guitarist Eddie Hazel to imagine that his mother had died before recording Maggot Brain’s almost ten minute long title track. Hazel transforms his guitar into a wailing and mourning instrument of grief. Beneath his solo, a dreamy, six note arpeggio acts as the bedrock to one of the greatest guitar performances ever captured on tape. “Can You Get To That” flips the energy from dark to light with its slick groove and doo-wop harmonies. A bright and joyous song at face value, the lyrics warn that even in death, no one escapes karma. “Hit It And Quit It” is a flamboyant acid rock tune with an odd metre that betrays Funkadelic's debt to both the church and the temple of Jimi Hendrix. For an outfit that proved so adept at conjuring colourful, funky images of utopia, it's curious that they chose to close out their greatest album with “Wars Of Armageddon”. Clocking in at over nine minutes long, the song is a minefield of explosions, screams and fuzzed-out guitars. The chants of “More power to the people/More pussy to the power” offer a reminder that Funkadelic’s psychedelic ideals and ambitions never strayed too far from the funky, carnal physicality of life on Earth. This review appears in The Wire 512 along with many other reviews of new and recent records, books, films, festivals and more. To read them all, pick up a copy of the magazine in our online shop. Wire subscribers can also read the issue in our online magazine library.
items._genre: psychedelic funk / experimental rock / acid rock / proto-punk
items._cn_summary: 《Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow》是Funkadelic在1970年发行的第二张专辑，在Jimi Hendrix离世后承接了黑色摇滚与迷幻音乐的脉络。George Clinton在录制过程中汲取地下漫画、黑人权力运动、激进左翼理论以及古代外星人假说的影响，将多种文化、历史与超自然元素融入LSD浸透的录音现场。专辑以Eddie Hazel粗粝的蓝调吉他与哇音踏板为核心，探讨金钱与自由的关系。结尾曲将早期作品《Open Your Eyes》倒放处理，将福音旋律扭曲为更晦暗的形态。开场曲长达十分钟，在失真吉他与宇宙合成器的音墙中展开迷幻音景，是70年代迷幻放克实验的代表作之一。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — More than a decade after releasing the fairly experimental 'Nocturniquet', The Mars Volta returnedwith a brand-new self-titled studio album, released by Clouds Hill in 2022. A brief hiatus and asecret 2019 reunion led to the formation of an updated lineup featuring the creative core of Omarand Cedric alongside bass player Eva Gardner, drummer Willy Rodriguez and synth player MarcelRodr�guez-L�pez. In what could only be interpreted as a creative reset for the band, 'The MarsVolta' represents a bold and spiritually moving art rock collection that sees the prog innovatorsplaying a warm and melodic combination of danceable Latin rock, neo-psychedelia with electronicundertones, and straightforward indie pop/rock. Undeniably this is the most radio-friendly versionof the band so far, whereas the writing of Omar Rodr�guez-L�pez sounds grounded, smooth, andconfident, and has little in resemblance with the unhinged experimentation that had marked The MarsVolta's earliest efforts.Catchy pop tunes and eerily atmospheric indie ballads prevail here, making this release aninteresting exercise in form and texture from a band known for its exaggerated rock-basedsoundscapes. Gentle Caribbean rhythms and layered ambient sounds provide an almost psychedelicbackdrop to the album, which is quite solid overall. What each musician is playing is clearlyidentifiable, and I find that clarity valuable in an experimentally inclined pop album, although I'mnot convinced that every part of the record works equally well. While you may find extravagant andexciting accessible tunes like 'Blacklight Shine', 'No Case Gain', 'The Requisition', or 'Que DiosTe Maldiga Mi Coraz�n', 'TMV' also features a good amount of watered down and forgettable trackswith an almost complete lack of rhythmic development like 'Cerulea', 'Shore Story', and 'CollapsibleShoulders', that for me add little to no substance to the record and on certain occasions seem to bemere tracklist placeholders. It is this disbalance between excellent and bland that must havestumped most listeners upon hearing this record for the first time, including myself. And while Iappreciate the uncompromising risk the band took with this album, I ultimately have to conclude thatthis is simply not their best work.
items._genre: art rock / neo-psychedelia / Latin rock / indie pop
items._cn_summary: 这是Mars Volta在沉寂十年后推出的同名回归专辑，由核心成员Omar与Cedric领衔，搭配新阵容完成录制。整体方向明显从早年的失控式实验转向温暖、旋律化的路线，融合拉丁节奏、新迷幻氛围与电子底色，呈现一种更具可听性的舞曲化摇滚面貌。评论者特别肯定了制作上的清晰度——每位乐手的演奏线条都易于辨识，这对一支实验倾向的乐队而言是难得的变化。然而专辑也存在明显的不平衡：'Blacklight Shine'、'Que Dios Te Maldiga Mi Corazón'等曲目展现出抓人的旋律与编排张力，而'Cerulea'、'Shore Story'等作品则显得节奏发展不足、流于平淡，削弱了整体统一感。评论最终认为这是乐队一次大胆但并非最成功的尝试，在自我重置与听众期待之间留下了模糊地带。

items.body: Los Angeles duo Patriarchy released an official video for “Lilylicker” on 29 September 2026. The track is the second song on the EP “Appendices,” released 7 August 2026 as a companion to the band’s 2025 album “Manual for Dying.” Appendices by Patriarchy The track opens on a low synth line and a steady kick drum, with Huizenga’s vocals half-whispered through the verses. The arrangement hardens into an industrial-techno beat partway through, with distorted guitars entering on the chorus. Patriarchy describes its own sound as “snuff pop,” a mix of metal, synthpop, punk and dance music. “Appendices” runs five tracks: “Bite Marks,” “Lilylicker,” “Servile,” “Ode (to an Apprehensive Tyrant)” and “Hate Fuck.” Huizenga and English wrote, performed, produced and recorded all five themselves. AJ English mixed “Lilylicker” and Enyang Urbiks mastered it. Witch Club Satan adds backing vocals on “Servile.” The EP is also out as a limited 12-inch clear vinyl edition of 300 copies, shipping around 1 November 2026, alongside digital formats on Bandcamp and streaming services. Patriarchy’s video for ‘Lilylicker’ Patriarchy directed the “Lilylicker” video itself, with cinematography by Hazel Hill McCarthy. Huizenga appears in a white gown holding lilies, then in a pink dress with chains and a metallic corset with gold wings; AJ English, also known as The Drummer, holds a skull and wears white wings. Huizenga’s son also appears in the video. The crew had to relocate the shoot outdoors to the hills above Los Angeles after the original studio balked at the concept and at having a child on set. Huizenga said the move improved the result: “A lot of the things that went ‘wrong’ ultimately added to the beauty of it, like having to shoot outside, where moths kept flying in front of our lenses.” On the project’s name and intent, Huizenga commented: “Patriarchy has never been about perfection, it’s about realizing we are the last remnants of human existence before AI enslaves us all; that’s why the project is called Patriarchy after all.” About Patriarchy Patriarchy formed in Los Angeles as a collaboration between Actually Huizenga and Andrew Means, who met when his band 3TEETH played a show at Das Bunker and offered to work with her in the studio between tour dates. Huizenga had been focused on filmmaking after a prior solo album, “Predator Romantic,” but the sessions with Means led the two to release the songs and build a band around them. Patriarchy released its debut album, “Asking for It,” on 8 November 2019 through Dero Arcade. The band built on that start with “The Unself,” released 26 August 2022, and “Manual for Dying,” out 19 September 2025 and trailed by the singles “Boy on a Leash,” “New Way” and “Die Like Everyone Else.” Patriarchy’s current lineup pairs Huizenga with AJ English, known as The Drummer. The band’s videos, including the earlier live performance clip “No Touch Torture,” are staged and directed largely by Huizenga herself. “Appendices,” the band’s companion EP to “Manual for Dying,” draws on Oscar Wilde, the Marchesa Luisa Casati, the emperor Tiberius and the Manson family as reference points. “Lilylicker” is the second single pulled from that EP, following “Servile,” and its video is Patriarchy’s newest visual release.
items._cn_summary: Patriarchy 是一支来自洛杉矶的二人组合，自称"snuff pop"，将金属、合成器流行、朋克与舞曲元素熔于一炉。《Appendices》作为 2025 年专辑《Manual for Dying》的延伸 EP，共收录五首作品，其中《Lilylicker》以低沉合成器线条与稳定底鼓开篇，Huizenga 的半低语人声贯穿主歌，中段转入硬化的工业 techno 节拍，副歌处加入失真吉他。整张 EP 由二人独立完成词曲、演奏、录音与制作，仅混音与母带交由他人处理，并限量发行 300 张透明黑胶。MV 同样由乐队自导，拍摄中遭遇片场拒绝、临时转场户外等波折，最终的山景与飞蛾入镜反而成为影像的有机组成部分。Huizenga 表示项目名称承载着对 AI 时代人类残余身份的认知，作品在工业声响与流行结构之间保持张力。

items.body: Label: Endectomorph Records, 2026 Personnel - Kenny Warren: trumpet; Adam Schneit: alto saxophone, clarinet; JP Schlegelmilch: organ; Andrew Dow: electric bass; Nathan Ellman-Bell: drums. Slow Tiger—the jazz quintet of trumpeter Kenny Warren, saxophonist and clarinetist Adam Schneit, organist JP Schlegelmilch, electric bassist Andrew Dow, and drummer Nathan Ellman-Bell—releases its debut album, pointing in many directions with an impeccable flow and assured tones. All its members, with the exception of Ellman-Bell, contribute compositions, filtering influences through the lens of this cohesive collective ensemble. Melodies stick on the ear as the band, whose prior successful collaborations led to the album, leans toward a pop/rock style that easily accommodates jazz-leaning improvisation. Warren's " Powerpuff Backpack " is a tribute to late trumpeter Ron Miles, revealing traces of folk and funk woven into the framework of pop and psychedelic rock infusions. Occasionally, bands like Inspiral Carpets and Jethro Tull come to mind, and Schneit's clarinet explores with effortless inside/outside agility, followed by Warren, who also brings in " Eleven Six ”. Its title comes from the fact that Ellman-Bell plays a cymbal pulsation in eleven while Dow shapes an upbeat six-beat bass figure that provides solid ground for the horn players to interact. They exchange ideas with grip and avant-garde stance, while Schlegelmilch makes the piece soar via hypnotic organ waves and ostinato-leaning textures that add dimension to the music. Schneit, who was born in Portland, Maine, named " Wharf Street " after the street where he grew up. This is a pop tune permeated with a strong 60's vibe, with the composer and Warren intersecting phrases with insouciant power, precision, but also freedom. They also bring this strategy to Schlegelmilch's time-shifting " Maritime Studies ”, which is buttressed by a sluggish beat and cautiously measured unisons. The organist's response to the pandemic's forced pause comes with " Mending the Nets ”, a gentle waltzing ballad moved by sizzling brushes, melancholic melody, and church-like organ sustains. The quintet aligns in relaxed sounds on the title track, " Slow Tiger ", a soulful, melodically seductive piece romanticized by warm R&B colors. It contrasts with Dow's " Funhouse ", whose groove in nine defines the tempo. With the organ illuminating the scenario with crested ripples of sound, the piece morphs into openly avant-garde territory as the horns criss-cross atop the rhythmic net laced by bass and drums. Slow Tiger shows potential, and its debut is a tantalizing promise of more albums to come. Favorite Tracks: 02 - Maritime Studies ► 05 - Eleven in Six ► 07 - Funhouse ► 09 - Slow Tiger
items._cn_summary: Slow Tiger的首张同名专辑由小号手Kenny Warren领衔的五重奏呈现，乐队以爵士即兴为根基，向多个方向探索。作品融合流行摇滚、迷幻摇滚、民谣与放克元素，但保留自由爵士的前卫姿态与即兴张力。Schlegelmilch的风琴铺陈出催眠式音浪与持续音纹理，Schneit的单簧管在内外即兴间自由游走，Warren的小号则向已故小号手Ron Miles致敬。编曲上运用复杂节拍，如《Eleven Six》中十一拍镲脉与六拍贝斯线条的交错，《Funhouse》以九拍律动进入开放式前卫领域。整体气质偏学院爵士与流行融合，而非纯粹实验或电子方向。

items.body: “Curandera” opens Bestiaria with a healer giving instructions. “Niña / Escucha cómo tu cuerpo te habla,” sings Ana Karen G. Barajas of Karen y Los Remedios: girl, listen to how your body talks to you. The song comes from Karen’s own illness and from the women in her family who saw her through it with advice, recipes and limpias, the cleansing rituals Mexican grandmothers pass down. The curandera in the lyric hands the work back to the girl, telling her to listen to her body and to how her soul breathes, and warns her that “Cuando callas te guardas / Lo malo / Y lo bueno”: stay silent and you keep the bad in with the good. Karen, guitarist Guillermo Berbeyer and Mexico City producer Jiony set it as a dark cumbia over a low bass and a steady beat. Trombone and cowbell sit around her voice, an organ hangs at the back of the mix, and in the instrumental breaks synth and guitar lines take over. She lives in Hong Kong now, a long way from the Mexico City she was born in and the Guanajuato she grew up in. Bestiaria, the follow-up to 2023’s Silencio, builds its twelve songs around twelve figures, among them the agave goddess Mayahuel and the Fates of “Las Moiras”. “Curandera” is the fourth single from it. items.body: Daydreaming, lost and found Daydreaming, nowhere bound Falling deeper, falling down, it took me over And I can’t get out The life inside your head has certain advantages: better dialogue, revised endings, people who finally say what you needed to hear. Spend enough time there, though, and the ordinary world begins to feel like an interruption. Somewhere between rehearsing a happier life and forgetting to participate in your own, the imagination acquires a troubling degree of authority. Minsk-based artist Tomorrows Letters traces that retreat on *Daydreaming*, a troubled synthpop lullaby set against a stark, black-and-white DIY video. The solo project of Kiryl Karotki, Tomorrows Letters gives the song an especially compelling frame: music that draws you close as its singer searches for a way out. A deep snare and a looping bassline establish a measured, insistent rhythm, with a low metallic synth figure moving beneath high, resonant chimes. The bells lend the opening a fragile sweetness, soon complicated by Karotki’s voice. Drenched in reverb, his baritone carries regret and despondency with considerable poise, allowing dread to gather beneath the melody. Certain phrases soften toward a tender whisper without losing their weight. There is a strong affinity with Dave Gahan here, particularly the sensual unease of Depeche Mode around Violator and Songs of Faith and Devotion. High harmonies brush the edges of the lead vocal, while a gentle acoustic jangle and deeper string tones add movement beneath it. Karotki gives these familiar pleasures a distinct arrangement: the bass keeps circling, the bells retain their nursery-room delicacy, and the voice seems increasingly conscious of how far it has drifted from safety. “The track was originally titled ‘Maladaptive Daydreaming’, and that’s the core of it,” Karotki explains. “It’s about that state where your inner world becomes so consuming that it starts to replace reality. It’s about how escapism can turn into a trap.” The lyrics trace that loss of control through thoughts taking flight in swirling formations, gathering a momentum their owner cannot arrest. A second voice has apparently dismissed the habit as a way to cope; the singer answers by describing the grip it has taken on him. The chorus keeps returning to the same admission, “And I can’t get out.” By the outro, the private entertainment has exhausted itself: the curtain falls, the screen goes silent, and an empty chair remains. Even then, the imagined story keeps calling. Karotki built the recording around sampled bass guitar and bells, producing it on two vintage hardware samplers running from floppy disks. His intention was to keep the sound firmly within 1980s synthpop, with the equipment lending its own worn texture to the arrangement. He then mixed the track with Andrei Bobrovka, known for his work with Molchat Doma and Nürnberg, and completed the cover artwork himself. The self-filmed video extends Karotki’s affection for classic Depeche Mode imagery into stark black-and-white rural scenes. He sits blindfolded on a chair in an open field; elsewhere, he performs with a guitar or peers through a screen of leaves. Flocks of birds fold and turn across the sky, giving the opening lyric’s murmuration a visual counterpart. The field offers room in every direction, yet the blindfold makes that freedom inaccessible. Images of the chair picked out by light against darkness bring the song’s final sense of vacancy into view. Watch the video for Daydreaming below: Working with a hardware-only approach, Tomorrows Letters draws on New Romantic pop and minimal synth to examine isolation, compulsive creation, and the less hospitable corners of the self. On Up Against the Wall, Karotki cast self-judgment as a trial with no prospect of acquittal. Daydreaming approaches that inward confinement through the comforts that gradually become dependencies, extending his interest in the mind’s capacity to make captivity feel familiar. The single also includes a remix by Farforovyekoty, the side project of Nürnberg’s vocalist, which gives the song a more aggressive, post-punk treatment. Besides the original’s uneasy lullaby, it offers another route into Karotki’s fixation. The invitation is gentle enough; the difficulty comes when you try to leave. Listen to Daydreaming via Apple Music or Spotify below: The single is also available for purchase on Bandcamp. items._cn_summary: 明斯克艺术家Kiryl Karotki以Tomorrows Letters之名发布单曲《Daydreaming》，探讨白日梦从逃避手段异化为牢笼的心理过程。创作以两台运行软盘的古早硬件采样器为核心，采样贝斯与钟声构建律动，男中音嗓音深陷混响，传递出疲惫与无力感。编曲上深沉的军鼓与循环低音线奠定节奏，高频共振钟声与金属合成器交织，高和声润色主唱人声，吉他与弦乐铺陈层次，整体向八十年代合成器流行致敬，同时与Depeche Mode式的阴郁气息一脉相承。黑白DIY影像延续音频的封闭感，独自录制强化了作品的孤绝气质。制作由曾与Molchat Doma合作的Andrei Bobrovka完成混音，封面亦为Karotki亲手绘制。作品在主题上直面想象力对现实经验的侵蚀，声音上保持复古合成器质朴质感，是一次内向而克制的表达。

items.body: My sins are all forgiven. I might be desperate, but I won’t let you forget. I know you will give in to me. I am dead set. I am dead set. She 1 • Him 2 have built their latest single Obsessed around one of pop music’s most reliable bad ideas: somebody confusing romantic destiny with a complete inability to take no for an answer. The Cleveland duo of Evan Nave and Cassie Bishop bring years of Lestat and Shy Moon behind them, though Obsessed feels leaner and brighter than that résumé might suggest. The synths skip forward in sharp little patterns, Bishop keeps her vocal airy and cool, and underneath it all sits an electroclash streak that brings to mind the clipped attitude and wiry pop economy of Elastica fed through a rack of 80s electronics. There is plenty of Human League, Yazoo, Soft Cell, and Ladytron in the bloodstream, but the guitars give the track an extra shove. Producer Michael Seifert threads in parts with a distinctly Fixx-like character, adding just enough bite to keep the arrangement from becoming too polished for its own good. “This song has been amazing to put together,” says Nave. “An 80s vibe with a very modern spin. And our producer, Michael Seifert, dropped some very Fixx-like guitars on it. Love the dark lyrical tone versus the upbeat music dichotomy.” That contrast is where Obsessed starts getting funny in a slightly alarming way. The music suggests somebody having a marvelous time under bright club lights; the lyrics suggest that somebody has already memorized your commute. Bishop drew inspiration from the horror film Obsession and its character Nikki, played by Inde Navarrette. “I wrote the lyrics to this song based off the movie Obsession, which I loved and thought was a unique and fun idea for a horror movie,” says Bishop. “I wanted to capture some of the elements and mood of the film in this piece.” She certainly found the right emotional neighborhood. The character at the center of the song barrels through pleading, certainty, possession, and total romantic entitlement while treating every objection as a temporary inconvenience. Love becomes less a mutual arrangement than a hostile takeover conducted in excellent makeup. Bishop wisely keeps her delivery light. She never overplays the menace, and that restraint makes the character more convincing. The voice remains smooth, composed, almost sweet, even as the lyrics tighten their grip. It gives Obsessed the unnerving quality of someone smiling pleasantly while explaining why the two of you are obviously meant to spend eternity together. The electroclash edge helps, too. Those angular guitars and bright electronics give the song a brisk, fashionable nastiness, somewhere between synthpop precision and the kind of deadpan cool Elastica once made look effortless. Obsessed is catchy enough to dance to and unhinged enough to make you reconsider sharing your location. Romance, apparently, remains a dangerous hobby. The charming video channels that same bubbly sycophancy inside the studio, where eager autograph and selfie seekers chase the performers around, hoping for — and eventually fighting over — a moment with their idols. There is something wonderfully silly about the escalation, and visually it brings to mind Toni Basil’s Mickey, with its bright, performative enthusiasm and choreographed fan frenzy. The joke fits the song neatly: admiration is only one bad decision away from fixation. Watch the video for Obsessed below: Listen to Obsessed below and order the single here. items.body: The Future arrived Tuesday No one knew, however A girl packing her suitcase saying, “Maybe now or never” There is a bassline in Ganser’s Futuretripping that seems to know the economy is fake, the clocks are lying, and somebody somewhere is trying to sell you another subscription to tomorrow. Around it, Brian Cundiff’s guitars jab and veer while Alicia Gaines sings with the cool composure of someone watching the machinery malfunction exactly as expected. The result lands somewhere between Bikini Kill, The Breeders, and DEVO, all wired together by a song obsessed with time, delay, and the peculiar modern habit of waiting for permission to panic. Futuretripping is a wiry, nervy post-punk offering built from elastic bass, restless guitar, and the kind of lyrical absurdity that makes modern life sound only slightly more ridiculous than it already is. Somewhere between The Breeders, Bikini Kill, and DEVO, the song turns anxiety about time, media, and collective hesitation into something sharp enough to dance to. The track picks up the rhythmic intelligence that ran through Animal Hospital, the band’s third LP, while pushing the tension into a tighter frame. The bassline keeps the song in motion with a thick, spring-loaded bounce, while the guitar scratches and darts around it with nervous energy. Alicia Gaines sings with a dry, controlled delivery that gives the song’s stranger images room to land without forcing the joke. The lyrics revolve around a world trapped in endless anticipation. Screens insist that everything is going according to plan, people wait for the next signal, and tomorrow becomes something they can apparently borrow from a shady acquaintance with the right connections. Ganser turns that uncertainty into deadpan comedy, presenting the future as another dubious commodity sold to people who have already spent too much of the present waiting around. The image of someone selling umbrellas beneath a clear sky gets at the song’s humor perfectly. It is ridiculous, vaguely ominous, and just believable enough. “Ahead of going on the road with Bikini Kill, I was interested in the concept of cheating time, where one could go for just a little more of it,” says Gaines. “After coming back from Europe earlier this year, we found our personal senses of time were distorted as we were dropped back into life in Chicago, mixing the mundane with the fantastical. Reaching into tomorrow for a little more of today became an inside joke, now Futuretripping.” Cundiff frames that temporal confusion as something closer to collective agitation. “Everybody’s waiting for the sign to change,” he says. “People tend to wait around to be fed what they should react to these days, what to do, and I suppose there’s a bit of that restlessness in the music and lyrics as well. It’s an agitation that it’s not tomorrow while also wanting more time today, right now.” Gaines also directs the accompanying video, which leans into a loose ’90s montage aesthetic, cutting random footage against the band performing beneath a bright blue sky. The editing has the same sideways humor as the song, constantly shifting between ordinary images and mildly surreal interruptions. Ganser leave us with a world where everybody is waiting for the sign to change while the sign itself appears to have wandered off. Watch the video for Futuretripping below: Chicago’s Ganser have spent the years since their 2018 debut Odd Talk developing an increasingly restless conversation between post-punk, noise rock, and art-school absurdity. Just Look At That Sky followed in 2020, while the 2022 EP Nothing You Do Matters brought Liars’ Angus Andrew into the producer’s chair. Bassist and vocalist Alicia Gaines and drummer Brian Cundiff remain central to the band’s writing, balancing physical rhythms with dry humor and an eye for the contradictions of everyday life. Their third album, Animal Hospital, was released through Felte on August 29, 2025, with production shared by Ganser and Andrew. A deluxe edition followed on April 22, 2026, adding five alternate versions of songs from the record. Touring with IDLES, Mclusky, and Ted Leo has helped sharpen their live attack; this September, Ganser joined Bikini Kill for shows in Milwaukee, Chicago, Royal Oak, and Cleveland. Futuretripping, released September 10, extends that momentum with a new song written and arranged by Gaines and Cundiff. items.body: Drone and Hum is not necessarily a new record – it was originally released five years ago, back in 2014, as a digital format. Now, as the year closes, this special album is released as a very limited 12” lathe cut vinyl edition, encased in a handmade sleeve and including a 6-page booklet. Photography from J.M Almqvist and a short story by Andrea Lundgren (which is written in Swedish) completes this delightful package. A stamped box includes the English translation of the story, along with an etched iron ore inside another bag. As if that wasn’t enough, 2 download codes for Drone and Hum and Drone and Hum Reworked are also included. The music is deserving of a beautiful physical release. Now, after a time, it has one. Old Amica’s sound is warm and comforting; wintry, but ultimately merry and bright. Chords are full and deep, resonating into the air and creating a sound that feels satisfied, complete, and whole. The music travels slowly, as if it were trampling through clumps of snow. Light tweaks take place here and there, altering notes, reversing them, and experimenting with the general flow of sound, but this never interferes or overtakes the music. The piano is still at the forefront, even with these subtle genetic mutations. Altered notes surround the main piano completely, not as a hostile act, but as a benevolent form of protection, an extra layer of warm clothing which adds to the sound rather than distracts or subtracts. The ambient sound billows out of ‘Solstrimman’ in a spectacular and utterly gorgeous way, and a place of spaciousness echoes throughout the album, where open, snow-coated fields stay untouched and villages are home to tiny populations. Although only making a brief appearance, a clean electric guitar adds some more colour with a warm, repeating melody. In the background, an ambient soundscape lingers and then covers the guitar’s sound in a gust of wind and dancing snow. The movements are almost balletic. The guitar is eventually lost in the ambient layer, shrouded in it completely. And the closing track ‘Eric’s Dinosaurs’ sees the homely piano return, and a thawing arrives with the birdsong. The piano is old, an elderly being, but it has aged like a fine wine, bringing musical maturity and sprinkling experience all over the record. There’s a lot of breathing space here, and as such, it’s a perfect album to close the year. Old Amica – Drone and Hum by Old Amica www.oscarson.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以钢琴为核心，结合环境氛围与微妙的音色处理，营造出冬日般宁静而温暖的声景。乐评详细描述了实体的精美包装，包括手工封面、瑞典语短故事及铁矿石等附赠物。音乐层面，钢琴旋律缓慢展开，音符经反转与变形处理，被环境音层包裹而非破坏，形成包裹式的保护感。电吉他仅短暂出现便被风雪般的氛围吞没，开阔的空间感贯穿全作。终曲以钢琴回归与鸟鸣暗示冰雪消融。整体制作偏轻柔冥想路线，具备一定的氛围实验性，但对追求前卫爵士、IDM或暗潮工业等更激进声音设计的听众而言，实验力度相对温和。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: Alison Cotton 的《The Gods Laugh》将民谣、前卫音乐与宗教氛围融合为一体。作品以中提琴、簧风琴、击弦古钢琴与钢琴为核心乐器，并加入鼓、贝斯与合成器拓宽音色谱系。多数曲目采用即兴方式一次性录完，整体笼罩在静谧、近乎神秘的气质中，缓慢的持续低音贯穿始终。John Clare 的诗作被谱以超脱的旋律，模拟古旧的民谣曲调；中段作品以中世纪圣咏般的开篇引入钢琴主导的简洁级进旋律。专辑同时也是对 Cotton 已故父亲的悼念之作，曲目中弥漫着失落与温柔交织的情绪，光与暗在不同段落中相互渗透。音乐难以被归入任何单一流派，最终以 Cotton 自身独特的艺术语言呈现。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."

items._cn_summary: 这不是一张传统意义上的音乐专辑，而是声音记录者伊恩·布伦南在芝加哥南区街道上录制的二十五位枪支暴力幸存者的口述声音档案。录音地点位于一位九十四岁祖母家前廊，靠近中途机场降落路径之下，环境声包括流浪狗徘徊、蚊虫嗡鸣与飞机轰鸣。部分参与者即兴说唱，多数为平民讲述自身经历，年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等。专辑保留了纯粹的街头声景，没有任何配乐添加。最令人印象深刻的是一位失去两个儿子的年长女性，她在叙述中反复道歉，而真正的歉意应来自社会对暴力的系统性纵容。专辑收益将捐赠给致力于以公共卫生方法终结暴力的组织。这件作品介于声音艺术与社会文献之间，实验性体现在其拒绝音乐化处理、坚持裸露现实声音的选择上。

items.body: Review by KansasForEver4 — Five years have passed since CASTANARC's rather mediocre *The Sea of ​​Broken Vows*, which featured eleven tracks ranging from three to five minutes in length?none of them particularly progressive in ambition. This time around, the approach is worlds apart from its predecessor: the album consists of just three tracks, with even the shortest one exceeding the length of the longest song on the 2021 release. One might well call this a "palace revolution"?a genuine surprise, as you can imagine.To appreciate CASTANARC, you first need to like Mark Holiday's somewhat distinctive voice?especially since the album is heavily vocal-driven, though the singing is superb. Yet CASTANARC is also defined by Mark Powell's multifaceted keyboards, which appear all over the album; there is plenty of piano, very little organ, and likely many sounds run through a Mellotron-style filter, with the smooth, fluid synthesizer work serving as the Doncaster band's trademark.We must also mention?lest anyone be overlooked?Neil Duty's excellent guitar work on the second track, "Ceasefire for the Innocent" (Duty previously appeared on the band's 1984 debut, *Journey to the East*, alongside Holiday and Powell); guest musician Dave Holley's contribution is equally impressive on the short "Cue Rain" (though at six minutes, "short" is relative); and the rhythm section?Peter Robinson on bass and Charlie Morgan on drums?delivers a solid, highly competent performance.While it doesn't break the mold with radical originality (remaining firmly within a very conventional neo-progressive vein), it is a fantastic surprise given the band's previous output.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑相较乐队前作是一次大刀阔斧的改革，从短小曲目转向仅含三首长篇作品的架构，时长大幅延长。乐队来自英国唐卡斯特，以Mark Holiday的人声为核心驱动，配合Mark Powell多变细腻的键盘铺陈，大量钢琴、少量管风琴及模拟Mellotron质感的合成器音色贯穿全作，构成其标志性的声音纹理。吉他手Neil Duty在第二首"Ceasefire for the Innocent"中有出色表现，特邀乐手Dave Holley在"Cue Rain"中亦贡献突出，节奏组稳定扎实。尽管整体仍深植于传统新前卫摇滚脉络，缺乏突破类型框架的原创性，但相较乐队既往平庸的输出，此作在结构野心与器乐编排上展现出明显提升，是一张扎实而具有回归水准的作品。
