items.body: La Feria returns to Liverpool this October for its eighth edition, spreading five days of Latin American music, theatre, dance, visual art and food from Hope Street down to Chinatown. The festival was launched in 2018 by Luma Creations, the Liverpool organisation led by Chilean-born songwriter Francisco Carrasco, to put artists from across Latin America and its British diaspora on the city’s stages. This year’s music starts in Chile, with songs built on the Andean rhythms of huayno and tinku and with folk tunes opened up through jazz improvisation. From there it moves to the brass-heavy mambo and salsa dura of a 13-piece Latin big band, to Afro-Colombian gaita flute set over electronic beats and deep bass, and to Brazilian forró and coco rhythms reworked as pop. Around the evening concerts and theatre performances, the week also brings a visual art exhibition, free workshops led by visiting artists, and two free family days to close the festival at the weekend. On Wednesday, Unity Theatre opens the festival with Manuelita, a one-woman show from Popelei in which Tamsin Hurtado Clarke takes on Manuela Sáenz. The Quito-born revolutionary fought through the independence wars at Simón Bolívar’s side, and in 1828 she helped him escape an attempt on his life in Bogotá. Hurtado Clarke tells her story through comedy and physical theatre to music by Colombian guitarist Camilo Menjura. Before the play, 18-year-old Argentine-British musician Eli Rowley plays Argentine and Andean tunes on the ronroco, a big-bodied, low-tuned relative of the charango, taking his cues from Gustavo Santaolalla and Jaime Torres. A short walk from Unity Theatre, the Music Room at Liverpool Philharmonic Hall takes over on Thursday, when Camila y Silvio return after selling out at La Feria in 2022. Camila Soria and Silvio Rozzi met during Chile’s student protests in 2011, and in 2015 they toured Argentina at length, learning the traditional styles of that country and the Andes. Their music moves between huayno, tinku, chacarera and vidala, with two voices over Rozzi’s guitar and charango and the deep thump of Soria’s bombo legüero. Fellow Chileans Peregrinos open the night. Guitarist Raimundo Santander and New York-based drummer Rodrigo Recabarren cut their first record together in Brooklyn in 2013, and they have used Chilean folk material as a starting point for improvisation ever since. By Friday the Music Room’s stage has to make space for thirteen musicians. Orchestra Mambo International came together in 2022 around Leeds salsa DJ Lubi Jovanovic and trombonist Jonny Enright to play the mambo of Tito Puente, Machito and Eddie Palmieri with a full big-band sound. Trumpets, trombone and baritone sax are stacked over piano, bass, vibraphone and a percussion section of bongos, congas and timbales. Since then they have written their own material, from mambos to cha-cha-chás, much of it gathered on their debut album Apúntalo. Up front, Venezuelan singer Carlos Peña, once a featured vocalist in Oscar D’León‘s orchestra, shares the vocals with Cuban singer Claritzel Miyares. It is the band’s first Liverpool show, and Cuban singer-songwriter George Peguero, returning to La Feria, opens the evening. Saturday night belongs to District, the club on Jordan Street in the Baltic Triangle, where Medellín producer Killabeatmaker sets Afro-Colombian and traditional Colombian rhythms over electronic beats and deep bass. His music keeps returning to the wildlife and landscapes of Colombia and the threats they face. On stage he beatboxes, raps and sings over live beats while Guadalupe Giraldo plays percussion and the gaita, the long, breathy duct flute of Colombia’s Caribbean coast. Opening the night, Mari Merenda plays her first ever UK show. The São Paulo singer/songwriter and producer built her name on videos of the asalato, a West African pair of seed-pod shakers knocked together on a cord. Her songs set forró and coco grooves against pop and R&B with electronic touches, most of them from her 2025 EP Reverbero. In Liverpool she switches between piano and asalato, with Guilherme Monteiro on bass, guitar and vocals, before moving on to Brighton and London. Before District opens its doors on Saturday night, World Museum on William Brown Street hands its galleries over to the festival for a free family day of music, dance, storytelling and workshops. The take-over is part of Cuerpos del Tiempo, a project with the museum’s Global Cultures Collections team to reimagine its Americas Gallery. Artists from eleven countries, from Argentina to Venezuela, perform among the displays. At midday Tamachij Chihuatl, a collective of more than 100 Indigenous Nahua women from Hueyapan in Puebla, Mexico, lead a food workshop. For forty years they have kept their village’s textile tradition alive, weaving wool and colouring it with natural dyes, and their name means “handmade”. La Feria’s free finale takes over The Black-E, the community arts centre on Great George Street, on Sunday. There, Orkney fiddler Catriona Price plays with El Guapo, a Buenos Aires duo on guitar, drums, percussion and vocals who mix Latin American roots with rock and funk. Together they run Routes to Roots, a project that brings musicians from different cultures together to write new music and rework traditional tunes, and which took them to the Edinburgh International Festival in August. Three dance companies share the day. London’s ArtPer UK bring Peruvian folk dances from the coast, the Andes and the Amazon, including the marinera norteña, a courtship dance in which couples circle each other waving handkerchiefs. Colibrí, a Manchester troupe of Mexican dancers led by Guerrero-born choreographer Magaly Flores, perform regional dances in traditional costume, from Veracruz and the Huasteca down to Oaxaca and Chiapas. Inti Tusuy, whose name is Quechua for “sun dance”, bring together dancers with roots in Bolivia, Mexico, Peru and the UK. Latin American food, DJs and dance workshops fill out the afternoon. Once the music stops at The Black-E on Sunday afternoon, the festival’s 2026 theme stays on the walls at Unity Theatre. Belonging, an exhibition by UK-based artists of Latin American heritage, runs there until 6th November, with work drawn from diaspora, ancestry and the places its makers call home.   Full programme and tickets are on the La Feria website The post Event Preview: La Feria 2026 (Liverpool; Wednesday 7th to Sunday 11th October 2026) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Sometimes, the band is the standout performance. What’s up, everyone! Welcome back to yet another installment of the J-Music Exchange/Rate! Your monthly source of Japanese music album reviews brought to you by yours truly and my good friend and fellow Japanese music fan Al from Omunibasu. If you’ve been rocking with us for a while now, then you already know the deal, but if this is your first time here and you’re not entirely sure what the Exchange/Rate is all about, please give the following primer a quick readーThe Exchange/Rate is a tandem album review series conducted every month by yours truly alongside my good friend and fellow Japanese music fan Al (from Omunibasu). Each month we decide on a specific theme with which our reviews would revolve around. We then pick out albums from our respective libraries which we think best coincides with that theme. We will then give the album we chose to the other person and vice versa (exchange), after which we then listen to and subsequently review the album we were given (rate). This project has not only allowed us to explore music beyond our libraries, but it provides an opportunity for us to see our favorite albums from a different point of view. It is our hope that this series is able to do the same for you and that you either find a new artist to try out and/or we offer you a fresh take on one of *your* favorite albums Al and I take turns deciding on a theme for our reviews every month, and for September we’re handing the reins back over to him. And I gotta say, I thought he came up with a pretty interesting one this time around, as we’ll be talking about albums that we feel exemplify an excellent group effort. Now, what exactly do we mean by that? Well, I don’t necessarily think it’s as simple as picking out an album where everyone involved is just really good at what they do. Rather, we’re looking at releases where you can genuinely feel the importance of everyone’s contributions to the finished work. Where the drums, bass, guitars, vocals, keys, production, or whatever else might be involved all feel integral to what makes the album what it is, and where taking any one of those elements away would leave you with something noticeably different. Of course, how that group effort manifests can vary quite a bit from one album to another, which is also what makes this such a fun theme to explore. For my pick, I went ahead and gave Al Fooocus by Aooo, a release that I think demonstrates the concept particularly well with how each of its members gets an opportunity to bring their own musical identity into the fold while still working together as one cohesive unit. You can check out what Al thought of that over at the Omunibasu Substack! Al, meanwhile, decided to send me Mani Mani by CRCK/LCKS, an album made by a group of musicians who, as we’re about to find out, have quite the collective pedigree between them. And perhaps more importantly for today’s discussion, they might just have a thing or two to teach us about what happens when you put that much individual talent in the same room. Let’s get into it! ーー CRCK/LCKS (クラックラックス) is a five-piece Japanese band formed in 2015, consisting of vocalist/keyboardist Oda Tomomi, saxophonist and multi-instrumentalist Konishi Ryo, guitarist Inoue Mei, bassist Ochi Shunsuke, and drummer Ishikawa Shun. Comprised of musicians with backgrounds predominantly rooted in jazz, the group brings together their respective expertise to create a style that freely moves between jazz, pop, R&B, and other contemporary influences, with an emphasis on intricate ensemble work and experimentation. ＜Ｍａｎｉ Ｍａｎｉ (まにまに)＞(＊Spotify link to the full album) CDJapan Affiliate Link(s):Mani Mani / CRCK/LCKS ＜T ｒａｃｋｌｉｓｔ＞ ０１・あらわらわ/arawarawa０２・レンタル神様/rental kamisama０３・真空パック/shinkuu pack０４・Psycho Sky０５・T.I.C.０６・沖に出たら/oki ni detara０７・枝と嵐/eda to arashi０８・バラライカ/balalaika０９・つまらない毎日/tsumaranai mainichi１０・Tiny Mirror１１・7月27日１２・You say goodbye１３・manimani Ａｌ：Ever since I first discovered CRCK/LCKS a few years ago, I’ve always found them to be a pretty fascinating band. It’s possible that I didn’t fully grasp what they were all about at first, but their two Temporary albums were ones I’d always come back to randomly, just because of how avant-garde the songs were and their overall irregular take on pop music. One moment you could be hearing a groovy cacophony of guitar, bass, and even the saxophone going wild, and another moment can have you getting lost in an ethereal soundscape. They may be a group that I have an on-and-off listening relationship with, but their ability to come up with this nutty stuff never fails to catch my attention. And I do feel like that’s why I came to enjoy their most recent album, Manimani, a lot. I’ll admit that the thought process for this month’s theme was based on how much more perceptive I’ve become when I listen to music, with me often trying to mentally separate the instrumental and/or vocal performances in a song, in order to really appreciate everyone’s efforts individually (and thus, understanding how well it all gels together). And with a band like CRCK/LCKS, who seem to display so many different elements in their music, it’s hard not to take interest in the mesmerizing or pleasant oddities they’ve been known for. Especially considering how varied the song selection is on Manimani, as the band showcases a more rambunctious side in the opener’s ending sequence (“arawarawa”), the unbelievably calming jazzy nature of “edatoarashi”, or how the bouncy and weirdly hyper traits in song like “bararaika” made it a standout song during my initial go-through with the album… it’s a record that feels very familiar if you’re an existing fan of the band, yet their efforts still feel super fresh with how surprisingly varied it is, style-wise. Another reason why I might’ve picked this one was because it’s described to be a cool celebration of CRCK/LCKS’ existence as a group, and every single member is featured on its songwriting credits. And after finding that out, it made it clear how much of a collective effort this album was, with everyone being able to chip in with their own ideas. And honestly, it resulted in an even more of an enjoyable experience. ーー Now, I actually thought about doing this one a little bit differently than I normally do for Exchange/Rate album reviews. If you’re a longtime follower of this series and are thus quite familiar with how I structure my end of the reviews, you’ll know that I typically pick out, at minimum, four songs from the album to talk about. These aren’t necessarily always my four favorite tracks either. More often than not, I use them to formulate a framework for how I want to approach the record as a whole; what I find good or intriguing about it, what I think the artist is trying to accomplish, and ultimately what kind of music listening experience I believe the album has to offer. In spending some time with CRCK/LCKS’ Mani Mani, however, I very quickly realized that I can’t really go about doing that here. Or, perhaps more accurately, I don’t think I should. Part of my reasoning for that is ultimately going to be at the heart of my overall thoughts on the album, but I think a good place to start this discussion is by first looking at the individual parts that make up CRCK/LCKS. Because if we’re going to talk about Mani Mani, I think we first have to talk about the people who made it. The band is led by multi-instrumentalist and Berklee College of Music graduate Konishi Ryo, known primarily within Japanese jazz circles for his work on the saxophone. Joining him on keys and vocals is classically trained Oda Tomomi, with jazz guitarist Inoue Mei on guitar, Ochi Shunsuke on bass, and Tokyo University of the Arts graduate and credentialed percussionist Ishikawa Shun behind the drums. For your everyday overseas Japanese music fan, I don’t necessarily expect all of those names to immediately jump off the page. For those more entrenched in the Japanese jazz scene in particular, however, seeing these five musicians come together in service of one collaborative project might read as something closer to a supergroup. Across the five members are numerous accolades and accomplishments within the Japanese music world, with each having established themselves through their own work and collaborations with renowned musicians both within and outside of Japan. All of which is to say that nobody in CRCK/LCKS necessarily needs the band to prove what they’re capable of individually. Everyone involved is already exceptionally accomplished at what they do. Which, naturally, begs a much more interesting question. What happens when you put all five of them together? That’s ultimately where my interest in Mani Mani lies. With this much individual talent packed into one group, it would be incredibly easy to approach the album by pulling everything apart and pointing toward what each member contributes. But I also think doing so would miss what makes CRCK/LCKS so fascinating in the first place. The question I’m more interested in asking isn’t what each of these five musicians can do individually. It’s whether what they create together amounts to something greater than the sum of its parts. Given how skilled everyone in CRCK/LCKS is with their respective instruments, I think it would be perfectly natural to assume that there’d eventually be some sense of one member overpowering another. Put five musicians of this caliber together and surely someone is gonna end up taking over the room, right? Except, as you’ll hear even from the opening stretch with Arawarawa, and subsequently thereafter with songs like Rental kamisama and Shinkuu pack, that never really happens. Instead, there’s this remarkable cohesion to the way CRCK/LCKS perform together where nobody sounds as though they need to tone down their own musicality simply to accommodate the other virtuosos playing alongside them. Everyone is still very clearly doing what they do best, only somehow without any of it coming at the expense of somebody else. You can still hear and appreciate Ishikawa Shun’s impeccable drum work without it ever distracting from Oda Tomomi’s lovely singing. Likewise, Konishi Ryo can bring his saxophone into the arrangement without completely stealing the spotlight away from Inoue Mei and Ochi Shunsuke on guitar and bass respectively. Nobody necessarily has to retreat into the background for somebody else to shine. And I think that’s an important distinction to make when talking about Mani Mani. The impressive thing isn’t simply that five extremely talented musicians are able to play well together. You’d probably expect that much given everyone’s credentials. It’s that they can seemingly play to the full extent of their abilities at the same time and still sound like a band rather than five individually impressive performances happening on top of one another. Part of me wants to simply chalk that up to the members being incredibly compatible with one another. At the very least, you don’t get the impression listening to Mani Mani that anyone feels the need to constantly prove themselves or overshadow everybody else in the room. But I do want to pose another possibility as to why CRCK/LCKS work so well together, and that’s the fact that all five of them come from jazz backgrounds. Obviously, there’s already going to be some preexisting overlap there. Having five musicians who operate within the same general musical space naturally gives them a shared foundation to work from. What I’m more interested in, however, is jazz itself and how the characteristics of the genre might have helped provide CRCK/LCKS with that unifying thread. Jazz is, by nature, a remarkably loose and unrestricted style of music. One of its most defining characteristics is improvisation, which inherently asks musicians to be responsive not only to what they’re playing, but also to what’s happening around them at any given moment. A performance can shift depending on what somebody else decides to do, leaving everyone involved to react and find their place within it. There’s a certain volatility to jazz in that regard, but I also think that’s precisely what makes it so conducive to having this many different elements operating at once. And perhaps that’s part of why CRCK/LCKS never feel overcrowded despite how much musicianship is constantly on display throughout Mani Mani. These aren’t simply five talented musicians who happen to be playing alongside one another. They’re five musicians coming from a musical tradition that, at its core, places a tremendous amount of value on listening and responding to the people playing alongside you. So when Ishikawa changes something on the drums, or Konishi comes through with the saxophone, or Inoue and Ochi start working something between the guitar and bass, everyone else has the musical vocabulary to respond accordingly. Their individual contributions don’t have to be planned around as obstacles; they become opportunities for everybody else to build upon. In that sense, jazz isn’t merely one of the styles that informs CRCK/LCKS’ music. It might very well be the reason all of these moving parts fit together as naturally as they do. In that regard, I do view Mani Mani as something closer to one big jazz jam session between the members of CRCK/LCKS more than anything else, and this is again largely why I decided not to approach this Exchange/Rate the way I normally would. Rather than viewing the album as a collection of individual songs and picking apart specific moments contained within them, I think Mani Mani works better as a showcase of what these five musicians are capable of creating together. It’s less about waiting for any one member to step forward and give you that big standout performance, and more about listening to how everyone continuously interacts with and plays off one another as the album moves along. Though there’s another side to that too, which is that there honestly aren’t that many singular moments throughout Mani Mani that I find myself wanting to isolate in the first place. And I don’t necessarily mean that as a criticism. If anything, part of what made it so difficult for me to pick out four songs to talk about is that the individual tracks themselves don’t really stand out that much over everything else on the album. There are certainly songs I enjoy more than others, with You say goodbye being the one clear exception for me as a song that I absolutely adore and would probably call my favorite track off Mani Mani simply for how beautiful it is. But beyond that, I rarely find myself listening to the album and thinking about one song being the song. Instead, CRCK/LCKS just… play. They create, they experiment, they respond to one another, and then they move on to the next idea. There’s a free-flowing quality to Mani Mani that makes the boundaries between those individual tracks feel considerably less important than the experience of hearing the band perform across the album as a whole. In that sense, listening to Mani Mani reminds me a lot of sitting down at a jazz bar and taking in a live set. You might walk away remembering a particular melody or moment that caught your ear, but that’s not necessarily why you enjoyed yourself. Sometimes the pleasure comes simply from sitting there and watching a group of incredibly capable musicians do their thing, seeing where the music takes them and appreciating how naturally they’re able to find one another along the way. That’s more or less how I find myself listening to Mani Mani. And perhaps that’s the best explanation I can give as to why, for once, I don’t really want to pull the album apart into four songs and tell you what makes each one work. The thing I find most interesting about Mani Mani isn’t any singular moment contained within it. It’s CRCK/LCKS themselves. ＜Ｗｈａｔ Ｉ ｔｈｉｎｋ ｏｆ Ｍａｎｉ Ｍａｎｉ ＞ So, after all of that, I suppose we’re left with the question that I posed at the very beginning: is CRCK/LCKS as a collective greater than the sum of its parts? Well… yes and no. If we’re looking at Mani Mani purely as a showcase of what happens when you put five incredibly accomplished musicians together and let them create, then I do think the answer is a resounding yes. There’s a level of musical understanding between everyone involved that allows each member to perform at an incredibly high level without ever making the album feel like a competition for your attention. Nobody gets lost, but nobody has to overpower everybody else either. Instead, their respective talents continually feed into one another, and I think the jazz background shared between them goes a long way toward explaining why that interaction feels as natural as it does. At the same time, I do think there’s another side to that equation when we start looking at Mani Mani specifically as an album. Going back to my comparison of listening to the record as being akin to sitting through a live set at a jazz bar, there are naturally opportunities for the mind to meander between songs. And I did find myself doing that here. There were a couple of times listening through Mani Mani where I noticed my attention starting to drift, only for the band to pick things back up instrumentally and pull me right back in again. Curiously enough, I almost wonder if that’s somewhat intentional. There are a lot of starts and stops throughout Mani Mani, along with these little interstitial tracks scattered between the more fully realized songs, to the point where it can sometimes feel like you’re supposed to lose track of exactly where you are in the album. One song ends, another idea comes in, the band pauses, something else begins, and eventually you look down and realize you’re three tracks further along than you thought you were. In most cases, I would probably consider that a knock against an album. After all, you’d generally want the songs themselves to leave enough of an impression that you can distinguish one from another. And as I mentioned earlier, outside of something like You say goodbye, there aren’t really many tracks on Mani Mani that I personally came away viewing as these huge individual landmarks. But I’m also not entirely convinced that Mani Mani wants to be experienced that way. The more time I spent with it, the less I found myself approaching the album as thirteen separate tracks and the more I started treating it as one continuous performance. Sometimes you’re completely locked in on what CRCK/LCKS are doing. Other times you let the music play while your mind wanders elsewhere. Then Ishikawa comes crashing back in on the drums, Konishi’s saxophone cuts through, Oda catches your ear with a vocal line, or Inoue and Ochi find another groove together and suddenly you’re paying attention again. And honestly, there’s something kind of pleasant about that. It makes Mani Mani less of an album where I’m constantly waiting for the next song I like to come on, and more of one where I simply enjoy spending time in the presence of the musicians playing it. The individual tracks become less important than the ebb and flow of the performance itself, which I think explains why trying to pick four of them apart for this review never quite felt right to me. So, is the whole greater than the sum of its parts? From a purely musical standpoint, absolutely. CRCK/LCKS are five tremendously accomplished musicians individually, but what makes Mani Mani interesting isn’t simply getting to hear all five of them demonstrate what they’re capable of. It’s hearing what each of them becomes in response to the other four. As an album, though, I think that same collective quality comes with a tradeoff. Mani Mani can be so free-flowing that its songs occasionally lose some of their individual identity along the way. But perhaps that’s also the point. Sometimes you don’t go to a jazz bar because you’re waiting to hear one particular song. Sometimes you go because the band is playing. ＜Ｍｙ Ｒａｔｉｎｇ＞４ ｏｕｔ ｏｆ ５ ＆ ８ ｏｕｔ ｏｆ １０ Mani Mani is, in a lot of ways, both memorable and unremarkable And I realize those two things sound like they shouldn’t be able to coexist, but I think that’s ultimately the best way I can summarize my experience with the album. Outside of something like You say goodbye, I don’t necessarily see myself walking away from Mani Mani remembering a bunch of individual songs or singular moments that completely blew me away. What I will remember, however, is the experience of listening to CRCK/LCKS play together. Because even during the moments where my attention started to drift, I don’t think there was ever a point where I questioned the quality of the musicianship on display. If anything, hearing five musicians this accomplished play alongside one another with seemingly very little interest in individually taking over the spotlight made me appreciate the collective that much more. Perhaps that’s also what makes Mani Mani such a fitting album for this month’s theme. When everyone involved is already this talented individually, it’d be easy for the appeal to simply become the novelty of hearing all of them on the same record. Instead, the most impressive thing about CRCK/LCKS is how quickly you stop thinking about any one member at all. ーー What are your guys’ thoughts on CRCK/LCKS’ Mani Mani? Let us know down in the comments! Likewise, what albums come to mind for you when you think of an excellent group effort? Whether it’s a band where every member feels integral to the music or simply a group of musicians who bring out the best in one another, we’d love to hear your picks! Lastly, before I let you guys go, don’t forget to check out Al’s review of Fooocus by Aooo over at the Omunibasu Substack if you haven’t yet! Happy Listening!

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — Still Thick As A Brick? Of course, this title evokes that of Jethro Tull's masterpiece, *Thick As A Brick* (TAAB for those in the know or the lazy), to which Ian Anderson himself gave a sequel 40 years later: *Thick As A Brick 2* (2012). *Still Thick As A Brick* isn't Tull's *TAAB* Episode 3, but rather the album by a new band led by Berlin-based Lutz Meinert?who also fronts the psychedelic rock band Margin?supported on acoustic guitar and vocals by Englishman Paul Forrest, a member of the Jethro Tull Experience, Crystal Palace guitarist Nils Conrad, and American flutist Ulla Hartmuth, whose virtuosity on the instrument rivals that of Ian Anderson. Despite nearly identical track titles (of course, it's a joke?), *Still Thick As A Brick* is neither a sequel to *TAAB* nor a simple cover of that legendary album. Just as TAAB told the story of Gerald Bostock, Still Thick As A Brick aims to tell the story of an inspiring figure: the famous financial magnate Georges Boston. Personally, I'd never heard of him, but as Reflection Club points out, to learn more about him, all we have to do is read what Rellington Stone magazine has to say?an entire issue of which is included in the CD booklet. Ha! Ha!Musically, there are plenty of similarities to TAAB, the most striking being Paul Forrest's singing style, with a slightly nasal voice very similar to that of Ian Anderson from the '70s. On *Still Thick As A Brick*, we also find that same playful flute that pops up at any moment, that same sense of rhythmic disruption, that recurring acoustic guitar developing highly catchy folk-rock themes, that anachronistic yet electrifying harpsichord, that delightful Hammond organ?worthy of John Evan's?an instrument particularly showcased on the exhilarating "The Foray of the Sharks " (5:37) or the very Tull-esque rock track "The Great Dance Around the Golden Calf" (3:35).Reflection Club intentionally set out to make an album "in the style of" and has succeeded in creating a thrilling work, close in spirit to TAAB (not to mention the very obvious nods) but one that manages to stand on its own, with some tracks less tied to Jethro Tull's '70s style. For example, the jazzy tones of "Nervesoothers" (3:10) place it more firmly between Camel and The Tangent. Furthermore, the contributions of guest musicians on sitar and violin, as well as a few brass notes (likely played on a synthesizer), judiciously enrich the atmosphere. And Reflection Club doesn't hesitate to vary the moods, stepping away from the bouncy symphonic folk-prog typical of Tull to embrace a tender pop-rock sound on the aptly named "Sentimental Depreciation" (5:19). Thus, after a few listens?from the magnificently symphonic "Prelude" (2:00) to the closing "Look Across The Sea" (4:24), a sort of sea shanty dominated by bagpipes?STAAB manages to make us forget TAAB for 48 minutes.So I have to admit that Reflection Club skillfully showcases more personality and originality than its album title would suggest. While it doesn't quite reach the creative heights of its brilliant and unsurpassed?more or less acknowledged?role model, Still Thick As A Brick captures all of its timeless charm, making for an undeniably enjoyable listen that should appeal to a wide audience, not just longtime Jethro Tull fans. And if Ian Anderson's TAAB 2 didn't quite win them over, they can safely give this Still TAAB a listen to make up for it.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由柏林音乐人Lutz Meinert领导的Reflection Club创作，明确定位为向Jethro Tull经典专辑《Thick As a Brick》致敬的作品。专辑沿用原作的曲目标题框架，讲述金融大亨Georges Boston的虚构故事，并附赠虚构杂志作为彩蛋。音乐上以原声吉他、笛子、风琴和竖琴为核心，复刻七十年代前卫民谣摇滚的弹跳节奏与交响编制，同时加入西塔琴、小提琴和铜管的点缀。Paul Forrest的鼻音唱腔刻意模仿Ian Anderson，Ulla Hartmuth的笛声技巧也呼应原作。部分曲目融入爵士元素和抒情人声，展示出一定个性，但整体仍是一张风格模仿之作，在实验性、声音设计的独创性上较为有限，更接近对经典作品的高完成度致敬而非独立的前卫创作。

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — Another really strong Procol Harum album, after their debut. Procol Harum is a great example of a less-is-more band, delivering strong music without being to complex or trying to be sophisticated. The music is piano/organ/vocal driven, the trademark Procol Harum sound, led by Gary Brooker and his warm, emotional voice. Matthew Fisher on the organ is again fantastic. The album is not loaded with guitar, but when Robin Trower comes in, he delivers some really tasty and artful sounds.I like all the songs here, and the highlight is the heavy psychedelic/progressive suite "In Held 'Twas In I" with classical and Eastern music influences.
items._cn_summary: 这是Procol Harum继首张专辑后的第二张唱片，被定位为Crossover Prog。整体以钢琴、风琴与人声为核心构建声音框架，Gary Brooker温暖且富有情感的嗓音是主导线索，Matthew Fisher的风琴演奏延续了其标志性的乐队音色。吉他成分被刻意压制，Robin Trower仅在需要时加入，贡献了若干细腻且具有艺术感的段落。专辑中所有曲目均受好评，最突出的作品是包含古典与东方音乐元素的迷幻/前卫组曲'In Held 'Twas In I'。乐评强调乐队奉行less-is-more理念，不过度追求复杂或精巧，而是以简练手法传递情感张力。该评论文本较短，缺乏更深入的技术分析与结构性讨论，信息密度有限。

items.body: Canadian electronic duo Delerium release their 16th studio album, “Exaudire”, on 22 January 2027 via Metropolis Records. The album arrives on regular CD and as a limited edition double vinyl pressed on oxblood-colored vinyl in a deluxe gatefold sleeve. The title “Exaudire” is Latin for listening, hearing and being heard. Metropolis Records describes the album as moving between the tangible and the dreamlike, built from electronic textures, expansive atmospheres and guest vocal performances. Side-Line previously reported on the album’s lead single, Into the Light, which embeds portions of Diamanda Galás’s 1986 recording “Deliver Me from Mine Enemies: IV. Ε Ξελόυ Mε (Deliver Me)” from her album “The Divine Punishment”. Exaudire by Delerium ‘Exaudire’ tracklist and guest vocalists The 12-track “Exaudire” features five different guest vocalists across its running order, confirmed via the album’s Bandcamp listing: “Higher Power” (feat. Mimi Page), “Into the Light” (feat. Diamanda Galás), “Dream Palace” (feat. Magic Wands), “Buried Light” (feat. Mimi Page), “Apocalypse” (feat. Inna Walters), “Stolen” (feat. Phildel), “Into the Unknown” (feat. Jaël), “Multiplying Zero” (feat. Inna Walters), “Chasing the Wind” (feat. Mimi Page), “Exaudire”, “Had to Go” (feat. Jaël) and “Litany” (feat. Mimi Page). Mimi Page is an American singer-songwriter and composer who has released four full-length albums since 2011. Magic Wands, a dream pop trio from Los Angeles, are also signed to Metropolis Records, with the albums “Switch” (2023) and “Cascades” (2025). Jaël, a Swiss singer, previously collaborated with Delerium on the 2003 EP “After All” and the album “Chimera”. Inna Walters, based in Nashville, already appeared on Delerium’s 2023 album “Signs”. Phildel is a classically trained English singer, pianist and songwriter from London. Delerium songs have previously appeared in the films “Brokedown Palace” and “Lara Croft: Tomb Raider”. “Silence”, the duo’s 2000 collaboration with Sarah McLachlan, was more recently heard in the BBC drama “Industry”. Side-Line also covered Peter Murphy and Boy George’s 2026 Delerium remix of “Let the Flowers Grow” and Restless Mosaic’s tribute track referencing the project. About Delerium Delerium was founded in Vancouver, Canada, in 1987 by Bill Leeb and original collaborator Michael Balch. Rhys Fulber later joined as Leeb’s main songwriting partner. Both Leeb and Fulber built their reputation in the electro-industrial group Front Line Assembly, and Delerium initially served as an outlet for dark, cinematic ambient soundscapes distinct from that project’s harder industrial sound. Early albums “Faces, Forms & Illusions” and “Morpheus” appeared in 1989. Through the 1990s, Delerium’s sound evolved from industrial electronics and ambient trance toward song-based electronic pop built around guest vocalists, a shift marked by 1994’s “Semantic Spaces”, which introduced a rotating cast of female singers on largely downtempo songs, a format the duo has used on every album since. “Karma” (1997) established Delerium’s more danceable side, and “Poem” (2000), produced with Chris Peterson, included “Silence” featuring Sarah McLachlan, which reached worldwide chart success and won a Juno Award in 2000. After the Leeb-Fulber reunion album “Chimera” (2003), Delerium continued through “Nuages du Monde” (2006), “Music Box Opera” (2012), the atmospheric “Mythologie” (2016) and “Signs” (2023), the latter featuring Inna Walters among other vocalists. “Exaudire” is Delerium’s 16th studio album and its first collaboration with Diamanda Galás.
items._cn_summary: Delerium 即将发布第十六张录音室专辑《Exaudire》，收录十二首作品，邀约五位客座歌手参与人声录制。专辑以拉丁语"聆听"为核心概念，在电子音景与梦幻氛围之间往返，加入小提琴家Diamanda Galás 1986年录音片段作为采样素材。厂牌Metropolis Records定位为独立暗潮电子厂牌，乐团成员Bill Leeb与Rhys Fulber此前在Front Line Assembly积累了电子工业背景。整体风格延续Delerium以氛围电子为基底、辅以人声点缀的路线。本次发表内容偏新闻通稿性质，缺乏对声音设计、曲式结构与艺术意图的具体分析，信息量不足以支撑深度评价。

items.body: Belgian electronic dance act Lords Of Acid release their new album “Mundo Bizarro” digitally on 15 October 2026 via Metropolis Records. LP and CD formats follow on 9 November. The album is the group’s first collection of new material since 2018’s “Pretty in Kink”. “Mundo Bizarro” gathers the four singles Lords Of Acid have issued since April 2026, Karaoke Superstar (featuring Princess Superstar), Dream Boy (featuring Carla Harvey), “El Mundo Está Loco” (featuring Tony & The Kiki) and Ich Will Nur Dass (featuring Mari Kattman), alongside seven further new songs. The full tracklist, confirmed via the band’s Bandcamp page, runs: “Dreamboy”, “Dancing on the Flames”, “El Mundo Está Loco”, “Dopamine War”, “Maximo Roboto”, “Ich Will Nur Dass”, “City of Angels”, “So Stoned Today”, “Karaoke Superstar”, “You’re Obscene” and “A Viking’s Heart”. Mundo Bizarro by Lords Of Acid Carla Harvey, formerly co-lead vocalist of the American heavy rock band Butcher Babies, joined Lords Of Acid in January 2025, succeeding the late Ruth McArdle. The digital release of “Mundo Bizarro” coincides with the second leg of Lords Of Acid’s Cheeky Freaky North American tour, first announced in February 2026. At that time, the album carried the working title “Acid Reign”. The September 2026 press release from Metropolis Records confirms the final title as “Mundo Bizarro”. Specific October and November tour dates were not included in the current press materials. About Lords Of Acid Lords Of Acid formed in Antwerp, Belgium, in 1988, founded by Praga Khan together with Oliver Adams and Jade 4U. The group emerged from the hard-edged electronic dance scene of that era, blending techno, acid house and industrial music with lyrics centered on sexuality, drug use and hedonism. The band debuted with the New Beat single “I Sit on Acid”. Its first album, “Lust”, followed in 1991. “Voodoo-U”, with Ruth McArdle on vocals, arrived in 1994 and brought a heavier industrial dance sound along with the band’s best-known US club hits. “Our Little Secret” appeared in 1997. The B-side compilation “Heaven Is an Orgasm” (1998) and the remix album “Expand Your Head” (1999) came next. The rock-influenced “Farstucker”, featuring Deborah Ostrega, arrived in 2000. After a long gap, “Deep Chills” (2012) introduced Mea Fisher on vocals, and the Kickstarter-funded “Pretty in Kink” (2018) introduced Marieke Bresseleers. Metropolis Records remastered and reissued the band’s catalog from 2017 onward. Ruth McArdle died in 2024. Carla Harvey, previously of Butcher Babies, was announced as the band’s new lead vocalist in January 2025 and has since toured extensively with the group, including the 2025 “Praise The Lords” tour and the 2026 “Cheeky Freaky” tour. “Mundo Bizarro” is Harvey’s first full studio album with Lords Of Acid.
items._cn_summary: 比利时电子舞曲组合 Lords Of Acid 宣布新专辑《Mundo Bizarro》将于 2026 年 10 月以数字形式发行，随后推出 CD 与黑胶版本。这是乐队自 2018 年《Pretty in Kink》以来的首张全新录音室作品，收录四首此前已发行的单曲与七首新歌共十一首曲目。新主唱 Carla Harvey（前 Butcher Babies 成员）于 2025 年加入，接替已故的 Ruth McArdle。乐队延续了自 1988 年以来的工业舞曲路线，融合 techno、acid house 与工业元素，以性、药物与享乐主义为主题。巡演与发行同期进行。本文为纯新闻发布稿，缺乏对音乐本身的评论与分析，未涉及制作细节、声音设计或艺术价值层面的探讨。

items.body: Ministry‘s “Moral Hygiene” turns 5 on 1 October. The industrial metal band released its fifteenth studio album through Nuclear Blast on 1 October 2021, produced by Al Jourgensen. The record runs ten tracks and 47 minutes, and it marked the first Ministry album since 2012’s “Relapse” to include a cover song. “Moral Hygiene” was recorded over roughly three years following 2018’s “AmeriKKKant” and is the first Ministry album to feature bassist Paul D’Amour, formerly of Tool, who joined the band in 2019. It is also the first record since 2006’s “Rio Grande Blood” without guitarist Sin Quirin, who left Ministry in March 2021. The album’s cover of Iggy Pop and James Williamson’s “Search and Destroy” was released as a single on 20 August 2021, alongside “Alert Level” (24 April 2020) and “Good Trouble” (8 July 2021), the latter accompanied by a “Unity Mix” the band put out to honor civil rights leader John Lewis. Guest musicians on “Moral Hygiene” include guitarist Billy Morrison, former Megadeth bassist David Ellefson, former N.W.A member Arabian Prince, and Jello Biafra, Jourgensen’s former bandmate in Lard, who takes lead vocals on “Sabotage Is Sex.” The album was engineered by Michael Rozon and mastered by Dave Donnelly. It was released on CD, vinyl, cassette and digital formats via Nuclear Blast. Moral Hygiene by Ministry About Ministry Ministry formed in Chicago in 1981 as the synthpop project of Al Jourgensen. The band’s 1983 debut, “With Sympathy,” was released through Arista Records and leaned toward the synth-driven sound of the era, a direction Jourgensen later disowned as label-imposed. Ministry’s sound shifted toward the aggressive, guitar-driven industrial style that would define the band starting with 1986’s “Twitch,” produced with Adrian Sherwood, and continuing through 1988’s “The Land of Rape and Honey” and 1989’s “The Mind Is a Terrible Thing to Taste,” both released on Sire Records. The band’s commercial breakthrough came with 1992’s “Psalm 69: The Way to Succeed and the Way to Suck Eggs,” which went platinum in the United States and included the single “Jesus Built My Hotrod” featuring Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers. Ministry continued through the 1990s with “Filth Pig” (1996) and “Dark Side of the Spoon” (1999), then released “Animositisomina” (2003), the final album to feature longtime bassist Paul Barker, before Jourgensen turned to a trilogy of albums aimed at the George W. Bush administration: “Houses of the Molé” (2004), “Rio Grande Blood” (2006) and “The Last Sucker” (2007). Jourgensen announced Ministry’s retirement after “The Last Sucker,” then reactivated the band with 2012’s “Relapse,” recorded after he survived a near-fatal ruptured ulcer. Ministry has released albums steadily since, including “From Beer to Eternity” (2013), featuring posthumous contributions from guitarist Mike Scaccia, “AmeriKKKant” (2018), “Moral Hygiene” (2021) and “Hopiumforthemasses” (2024), each addressing the political landscape of its release year. Jourgensen remains the band’s sole constant member, working alongside a rotating cast of musicians including longtime guitarist Cesar Soto and, since 2019, bassist Paul D’Amour. “Moral Hygiene” extended that run five years ago this October, arriving as Ministry’s fifteenth studio album.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非乐评，而是Ministry乐队第15张录音室专辑《Moral Hygiene》发行五周年的资讯性回顾。内容以编年史方式罗列专辑的基本事实：发行厂牌、制作人、曲目数量、客座乐手（包含Jello Biafra、David Ellefson等）以及成员变动。该专辑是乐队自2012年以来首次收录翻唱曲（Iggy Pop的《Search and Destroy》），录制历时约三年，制作人为Al Jourgensen。文中还概述了乐队从1981年芝加哥合成器流行起步、转向吉他驱动的工业金属风格、1990年代商业巅峰及随后多次重组的历史脉络。作为Side-Line刊发的资料性文章，缺乏对音乐本身的声音设计、创作手法或艺术价值的分析与评论。

items.body: Wumpscut’s eighth studio album, “Wreath of Barbs,” turns 25 this year. The German electro-industrial project released the record on 1 October 2001 through Beton Kopf Media in Germany, with Metropolis Records issuing the US edition on 9 October 2001. Wumpscut is the recording name of Bavarian musician Rudy Ratzinger, who wrote, arranged, performed, mixed and mastered the album himself. “Wreath of Barbs” runs eleven tracks: “Opening the Gates of Hell,” “Deliverance (Album Mix),” “Wreath of Barbs (Album Mix),” “Dr. Thodt,” “Mankind’s Disease,” “Christfuck,” “Troops Under Fire,” “Line of Corpses,” “Hate Is Mine,” “Bleed in Silence” and a remix of Kirlian Camera’s “Eclipse,” titled “Eclipse (Kaelte Container Remix).” Aleta Welling contributes female vocals and wrote the lyrics for “Wreath of Barbs” and “Dr. Thodt.” The album peaked at #13 on the CMJ RPM Chart in the US. Exclaim! described it as “a celebration of darkness and foreboding” and praised “Ratzinger’s talent for writing a catchy song.” Concurrent with the release, Ratzinger ran a remix contest for the title track, providing samples through his website and inviting any musician to submit a version for a chance at inclusion on the subsequent “Wreath of Barbs” MCD. The album has since seen multiple reissues, including a 2017 “Concentrated Camp Edition” and a DAT edition, and Wumpscut announced vinyl reissues of “Wreath of Barbs” and “Body Census” in December 2021. About Wumpscut Wumpscut, stylised as :wumpscut:, is a gothic-influenced electro-industrial project founded in Munich, Bavaria, in May 1991 by DJ Rudy Ratzinger, born Rudolf Ratzinger in 1966 in Gangkofen, West Germany. Ratzinger has remained the project’s sole member throughout its history, occasionally bringing in guest contributors such as vocalist Aleta Welling. He has cited the early work of Leæther Strip as his reason for moving from DJing to recording, saying in a 1997 interview that he “was a DJ for several years and was tired of offering the audience only alien stuff.” Wumpscut’s first release was the demo cassette “Defcon” in late 1991, followed by the project’s first full-length album, “Music for a Slaughtering Tribe,” in 1993. That album’s track “Soylent Green” drew early attention in goth and industrial club circuits in Germany, the UK and the US. Wumpscut released “Bunkertor 7” in 1995 and “Embryodead” in 1997, the latter reaching #20 on the CMJ RPM chart. The 1999 album “Boeses Junges Fleisch,” built around the life of German serial killer Fritz Haarmann, reached #25 on the CMJ RPM chart and #17 on the German Alternative Charts. The 2000 EP “Blutkind” followed, reaching #5 on the DAC Top 50 Albums of 2000 in Germany and #17 on the CMJ RPM chart in the US. Ratzinger started his own label, Beton Kopf Media, in 1995 to release Wumpscut material to the European market, and later ran the label Mental Ulcer Forges. “Wreath of Barbs,” released in 2001 through Beton Kopf Media in Germany and Metropolis Records in the US, reached #13 on the CMJ RPM Chart, the project’s highest US chart placement to date. Wumpscut has continued releasing albums since, including “Wüterich” (2016), “Fledermavs 303” (2021), “Schlossgheist” (2024) and “Chew Chew Chew” (2025), while remaining a studio-only project that has never toured. Twenty-five years on, “Wreath of Barbs” remains one of the project’s most commercially successful releases.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非真正意义上的乐评，而是一篇以纪念专辑发行25周年为框架的资讯性回顾。文章系统梳理了Wumpscut第八张录音室专辑《Wreath of Barbs》的曲目列表、发行厂牌、合作者（女性人声Aleta Welling参与两首歌曲的歌词创作）、商业成绩（在美国CMJ RPM榜单上达到第13位），以及专辑前后的项目历史与后续再版情况（包括2017年的"Concentrated Camp Edition"和DAT版本）。文章提及媒体Exclaim!的评价——将其描述为"对黑暗与不祥感的庆典"，并肯定了Ratzinger创作朗朗上口歌曲的才能，但缺少对具体音乐结构、声音设计或制作手法的深入分析。整体以项目沿革和发行信息为主，听感层面的评论极为有限，更接近厂牌宣传或维基百科式的条目整理，而非具有独立观点的乐评。

items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于日本爵士钢琴家海野雅威致敬Oscar Peterson名盘《We Get Requests》公演的新闻稿。海野自幼受Peterson影响立志成为爵士钢琴家，此次与贝斯手楠井五月及鼓手后藤龙太郎组成三重奏，在东京有乐町的I'M A SHOW演出该专辑相关曲目。演出的核心在于以海野个人视角重新诠释经典专辑中的乐曲，保留原专辑的摇摆感同时融入自身表达。作为生日与Peterson相同的钢琴家，海野也回顾了自身与Peterson鼓手Jeff Hamilton的渊源。文章内容偏资讯性质，缺乏对音乐本体的深度分析，且该演出属于主流爵士范畴，与实验、前卫或电子融合方向距离较远。

items.body:
CLOSE YOUR EYES have dropped their fourth mini album, 256th Note, alongside a music video for ‘Drop That!’.

Released on 30 September, the seven-track project follows the K-pop boy group’s 2025 EP blackout and sees them expand their sound through jazz-inspired improvisation, hip-hop, R&B, electropop, bossa nova, and more.

Taking inspiration from the spontaneity of jazz, 256th Note centres on capturing emotions as they occur rather than containing them within conventional forms. Its title references the 256th note, one of the shortest possible moments in music, as a reflection of the fleeting and unfiltered emotions found in everyday life. The album's seven tracks also mirror the seven-note musical scale.

The record opens with ‘Open Your Eyes’, an experimental meeting of jazz improvisation, hip-hop, and R&B featuring pianist Yohan Kim and saxophonist Jacob Scesney. ‘Drop That!’, meanwhile, reinterprets Yoon Si-nae’s ‘이 밤을 즐겁게’, described as an early example of Korean jazz funk, through 1990s street hip-hop and sampling. Its accompanying music video was released alongside the album.

Elsewhere, ‘Vibe Check’ pairs piano, restrained bass, and groovy drums with the members’ vocals and rap, while ‘Slowly Bleed’ moves between contemporary pop, electropop, and alternative R&B. ‘Fool For You’ leans into vintage-inspired R&B and lo-fi textures, while ‘Baby Bossa Nova’, featuring rising R&B artist Joo Hyerin, draws from traditional Brazilian bossa nova.

The album closes with ‘Eternity’, a pop ballad featuring lyrics written with participation from all seven members. Built around acoustic piano and vocals, the song expresses the group’s feelings towards their fans, CLOSER.

Formed through PROJECT7, CLOSE YOUR EYES comprise JEON MINWOOK, MA JINGXIANG, JANG YEOJUN, KIM SUNGMIN, SONG SEUNGHO, KENSHIN, and SEO KYOUNGBAE. Since debuting in April 2025, the group’s debut mini album ETERNALT sold 316,000 copies in its first week, while follow-up Snowy Summer surpassed 200,000 copies on its first day. Their debut focus track, ‘All My Poetry’, also earned the group their first music show win nine days after debut.

Led creatively by executive producer and creative director Lee Haein, CLOSE YOUR EYES continue to broaden their musical palette on 256th Note, turning brief moments of emotion into a seven-track snapshot of the group’s evolving sound.

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — Leviathan, an Italian outsider on the neo-prog scene who emerged in the late 1980s in the shadow of the genre's leading acts (Marillion, IQ, Pendragon, Pallas?), returns today in top form and highly motivated with *Heartquake/Redux*, a re-recorded version of their debut album, *Heartquake* (1988), while also planning the upcoming release of a brand-new album titled *Testudo*, which we'll be sure to discuss further when the time comes.A true manifesto of hyper-melodic, sensitive, and energetic neo-prog?with its sights set on the best of Genesis from the '78?'80 period?*Heartquake* is a resounding success, despite having been recorded under precarious conditions (in barely a week and on a shoestring budget). Andrea Amici, the keyboardist and principal composer of the current Leviathan lineup, didn't join the band until their second album, *Bee Yourself* (1990)?a record that's nearly impossible to find these days and deserves at least a reissue. Amici quickly became the principal composer alongside singer-songwriter Alex Brunori and longtime drummer (who also plays bass) Andrea Monetta. In this role, Amici appears to be the architect of the band's musical shift, moving from the English-flavored neo-prog of *Heartquake* to the more personal RPI sound of the third album, *Volume* (1997), with Paolo Antinori replacing Brunori on vocals. Since the album failed to achieve commercial or critical success?which, in my opinion, is regrettable and unfair (Volume deserves to be revisited and vindicated if necessary), Amici and Monetta then put the "monster" to sleep.It wasn't until the mid-2000s that Leviathan resurfaced, with two dazzling, lengthy suites composed by Amici in the vein of modern symphonic RPI, which were incorporated into projects by the Finnish collective Colossus: "Un Pensiero e Sempre Libero" (26:34) in 2005 and "Vecchi Giochi" (21:00) in 2008. These two grandiose pieces, sung in Italian (by Paolo Antinori on the first, then Pierfrancesco Drago and Rossella Salvucci on the second), are teeming with a succession of haunting melodic themes linked together with disconcerting brilliance, evoking the enchanting power of Samurai of Prog's finest moments; they likely represent Leviathan's most remarkable work to date.Since then, we've heard nothing more from Leviathan, but we've been able to console ourselves by following the career of Andrea Amici, who has never stopped composing and producing albums of primarily instrumental music, spanning genres as varied as classical piano (Romantic or Baroque) and electro, without ever completely severing ties with his love for progressive rock. Electronica was very much on the agenda last year with his latest solo album, *The Eye of the Storm*, performed entirely on keyboards?a result quite close to the best and most memorable recent work by Rick Wakeman and Tangerine Dream, enhanced with an irresistible touch of sunny RPI.Probably?and quite legitimately?capitalizing on the current resurgence in popularity and interest in neo-prog among prog fans, Amici and Monetta?this time with the return of singer Brunori?have managed to resurrect Leviathan from its still-hot ashes. But before presenting us with their brand-new compositions, the Roman band chose to remind us of their legacy with *Heartquake/Redux*, a reinterpretation of *Heartquake* that benefits from a bit more recording time and modern technological resources, designed to amplify the album's original qualities. The original compositions thus take on the luster they deserved, stripped of the overly 80s-style sound of the original. With the help of two other heavyweights of Italian prog?guitarist-producer Fabio Serra, leader of R�senkre�tz, and bassist Andrea Castelli, currently involved in the comeback of Il Rovescio Della Medaglia?Leviathan showcases one of its strongest sides: the guitars, as lyrical as ever, have become sharper; the keyboard sound has gained in clarity and maturity; Monetta's playing is more subtle yet just as powerful; and Brunori's voice hasn't suffered too much from the passage of time. One can only regret the absence of the last two tracks from *Heartquake*. Indeed, the very Hackett-esque instrumental "There's Only Watershade", and "In the Dream of Up We Quake!," a studio live recording (featuring Amici on keyboards) from the *Bee Yourself* sessions in '89, which was later included as a bonus track on the CD edition of *Heartquake*.But is this little facelift enough to make *Heartquake/Redux* a must-have for those who own and appreciate the original version? I'll leave it to the readers concerned to come up with an answer. For everyone else, *Heartquake/Redux* is an excellent opportunity to discover one of the jewels of Italian symphonic neo-prog?a band with undeniable potential and obvious artistic qualities, but one that history and a lack of commercial success have not sufficiently brought to light.For my part, I hope that Testudo, their next studio album, will combine the technical prowess of *Heartquake/Redux* with the inventiveness and melodic exuberance of the two suites Leviathan released in the 2000s.
items._cn_summary: 乐评聚焦意大利新前卫摇滚乐队Leviathan的重新录制专辑《Heartquake/Redux》，同时回顾乐队自1988年以来的演变历程。原版专辑在一周内以极低成本录制成型，被视为英式新前卫风格的宣言，风格指向七十年代末至八十年代初Genesis的黄金时期。乐评详述了核心成员Andrea Amici在音乐方向上的主导作用——从英式新前卫逐步转向更具个人色彩的意大利前卫摇滚（RPI）路线，并提及他为芬兰集体Colossus创作的两部长篇组曲，称其为乐队最佳作品。文章还讨论了Amici个人独奏作品中跨越古典钢琴与电子音乐的多元尝试。该文为典型的乐评人背景梳理与作品历史考据型评论，信息密度较高，但对专辑《Heartquake/Redux》本身的音乐分析被大量乐史叙述所稀释，文末似有截断。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Pink Floyd早期探索阶段的产物，处于从迷幻摇滚向太空摇滚过渡的关键时期。评论者认为专辑整体冗长乏味，难以完整聆听，唯有开场曲《Let there be more light》展现一定潜力。评论中认可《Set the controls for the heart of the sun》的表现，并特别提及终曲的管风琴段落为专辑唯一亮点。尽管评论者给出两星评价，但专辑本身在实验性音效、迷幻氛围营造和即兴器乐展开方面仍有探索价值，反映了乐队在Syd Barrett离队前后的创作转型。对于偏好前卫与实验音乐的听众而言，这张专辑可作为了解Pink Floyd早期发展脉络的参考，但评论本身的负面倾向影响了推荐度。

One major change in the bands line-up is the addition of new vocalist Aurelio Fierro. Former singer Marco Basile had a fantastic rang
items.body: Review by martindavey87 — 'Pulse For a Graveheart' is the second studio album by Italian progressive metal band Mind Key. Released in 2009, the group has shown a significant improvement over the four years that had passed since their debut, with stronger writing and a better-sounding production, a high quality is consistently maintained throughout the album. One major change in the bands line-up is the addition of new vocalist Aurelio Fierro. Former singer Marco Basile had a fantastic range, but at times his voice seemed quite tinny, whereas Fierro's powerful voice fits more comfortably with the music, adapting for soft, melodic sections or heavier, more aggressive parts. As expected with this genre, the musicianship is fantastic as always, featuring plenty of great interplay between all the instruments, with particular praise going to guitarist Emanuele Colella and keyboardist Dario De Cicco. There's also guest appearances by the likes of keyboard maestro Derek Sherinian, Tom Englund (of Everygrey fame), and Winger's Reb Beach.With highlights including 'Sunset Highway', 'Dead Fame Hunter', 'The Seventh Seal', 'Citizen of Greed' and 'Graveheart', this is a solid progressive metal album and sure to please all fans of the genre.
items._cn_summary: 意大利前卫金属乐队 Mind Key 于 2009 年发行的第二张录音室专辑，相比四年前的首作在作曲水准和制作质量上均有明显提升。新主唱 Aurelio Fierro 的嗓音较前作更为有力厚实，能够在柔美段落与激昂段落之间自如切换，与器乐编排的契合度更高。器乐演奏保持了一贯的高水准，吉他手 Emanuele Colella 与键盘手 Dario De Cicco 之间的互动尤为突出，另有 Derek Sherinian、Tom Englund、Reb Beach 等客座乐手参与。《Sunset Highway》《Dead Fame Hunter》《The Seventh Seal》《Citizen of Greed》《Graveheart》等曲目是专辑的亮点。整体而言，这是一张品质稳定的前卫金属作品，在该类型框架内完成度较高，但并未展现出超越类型惯例的实验性或跨界元素。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑的核心是为Charlie Rees的编曲作品而专门组建的大乐队项目，Martin Speake担任中音萨克斯独奏。Rees是Speake的前学生，同时也是萨克斯演奏者，他在原有谱面基础上进行了深度再创作，使管乐编制呈现更为丰满的层次感。文章聚焦于编配层面的技术解析，描述了编曲从原稿到成品的演变过程，以及大乐队编制如何作为载体承载这些重新编排的曲目。整体属于学院派爵士框架内的改编作品，强调管乐编制与谱面写作的配合，而非自由即兴或先锋实验路线。

items.body: A Rammstein producer, a string section and a major label: Covenant made their fifth album under different conditions from the four before it. Ka2 Music, a division of Sony Music, released “Northern Light” in Europe on 30 September 2002, and Metropolis Records followed in the United States on 8 October 2002. The Swedish futurepop trio from Helsingborg had spent its previous albums on the independents Memento Materia, Off Beat and Dependent Records. The album turns 24 this year. Jacob Hellner, who had produced Rammstein’s first three albums, produced “Northern Light” after pre-production by the band. Stefan Glaumann mixed “Call the Ships to Port”, “Bullet”, “Invisible & Silent” and “Prometheus”, Ulf Kruckenberg mixed the other seven tracks, and Björn Engelmann mastered. Axwell added programming, Ricard Nettermalm played live drums and Lizzie Zachrisson sang backing vocals on “Bullet”, “Scared” and “Atlas”. The Stockholm Session Orchestra, arranged and conducted by Joakim Milder, played the strings on “Invisible & Silent”, and Ulf Ivarsson played bass on “Atlas”. Joakim Montelius wrote the lyrics for seven tracks and Eskil Simonsson for five. “Rising Sun” carries a co-writing credit for American techno producer Steve Stoll and uses elements of his tracks “Reciproheat” and “Falling Down”. The eleven tracks run 58 minutes and 39 seconds: “Monochrome”, “Call the Ships to Port”, “Bullet”, “Invisible & Silent”, “Prometheus”, “We Stand Alone”, “Rising Sun”, “Winter Comes”, “We Want Revolution”, “Scared” and “Atlas”. Ka2 issued the album as a standard CD, a limited digipak CD and a numbered gatefold double vinyl of 1,000 copies. The vinyl added four tracks not on the CD: club versions of “Bullet” and “Call the Ships to Port”, “Bullet (Funky Indian)” and “Don’t Go”. The Sony CDs carried copy protection and a label reading “Auf PC/Mac nicht abspielbar”, and early copies came with a sticker listing the “Northern Light” tour dates. Metropolis pressed its US edition as an HDCD. Two singles bracketed the release. “Call the Ships to Port” came out on 12 August 2002 as a CD maxi with remixes by Oliver Klitzing, Christian Morgenstern, Kaylab and Thomas P. Heckmann, and reached number 93 on the German singles chart. “Bullet” followed on 9 December 2002 with an Ellen Allien “Flow Mix”, a Le Dust Sucker mix and the otherwise unreleased “Atom Heart”. A “Bullet” DVD with the video and making-of footage appeared in January 2003. About Covenant Eskil Simonsson, Joakim Montelius and Clas Nachmanson, three school friends from Helsingborg in southern Sweden, started making music together in 1986 after seeing Front 242’s first Scandinavian show, and took the name Covenant in 1988. They built a studio in Nachmanson’s bedroom while studying in Lund. Their first released track, “The Replicant”, appeared on a Memento Materia compilation in 1992, and the label issued the debut album “Dreams of a Cryotank” in December 1994. Off Beat signed the trio in 1995 after a German festival appearance. “Sequencer” followed in May 1996, with the “Stalker” single and a tour alongside Haujobb and Steril later that year. San Francisco label 21st Circuitry handled the United States, where the “Theremin” EP appeared in 1997. “Europa” came out in April 1998. When Off Beat closed in 1999, Covenant moved to the newly formed Dependent Records in Germany and SubSpace Communications in Sweden, while Metropolis Records took over the American catalogue. “United States of Mind” appeared in February 2000, with the “Der Leiermann” single, and the live album “Synergy” followed in November 2000. “Northern Light” moved the band to Sony’s Ka2 division in 2002. By then Montelius lived in Barcelona and Simonsson in Berlin, with Nachmanson still in Helsingborg. “Skyshaper” arrived in March 2006, and in March 2007 the band announced that Nachmanson would no longer tour, with Daniel Myer of Haujobb taking his place on stage. The tour film “In Transit” came out on DVD in October 2007 and confirmed Nachmanson’s departure. “Modern Ruin” followed in January 2011, the first album with Myer as a full member, and Daniel Jonasson joined the live line-up that year. Andreas Catjar joined in 2013 on keyboards and guitar, playing on “Leaving Babylon” in September 2013 and on “The Blinding Dark”, released on 4 November 2016 after the “Sound Mirrors” single. Montelius told Side-Line at the time that the line-up had grown to five, and that “Covenant’s basic principle is to always evolve: change is the only constant.” The band handed out the “Fieldworks: Exkursion” EP on its German tour in February 2019 and released a cover of Yazoo’s “Winter Kills” in December 2020. Andreas Catjar-Danielsson died on 29 July 2024 after a long illness, and the charity “Andreas EP”, recorded with Simonsson, came out on Dependent Records on 17 October 2025. Twenty-four years after Ka2 pressed it, “Northern Light” remains the album that brought “Call the Ships to Port” and “Bullet” into the Covenant catalogue.
items._cn_summary: 瑞典乐队Covenant的第五张专辑《Northern Light》由曾为Rammstein制作前三张专辑的Jacob Hellner担纲制作，乐队完成预制作后交由其操刀。专辑由索尼音乐旗下Ka2发行，标志着乐队首次进入大型主流唱片公司体系。制作团队包括混音师Stefan Glaumann与Ulf Kruckenberg，母带由Björn Engelmann处理，斯德哥尔摩弦乐团在Joakim Milder指挥下为《Invisible & Silent》录制弦乐部分。乐队成员Joakim Montelius负责七首曲目的歌词，Eskil Simonsson负责另外五首。专辑共收录十一首曲目，另有四首额外曲目收录于限量黑胶版本。整体制作规格较高，但作为futurepop/EBM类型作品，其风格定位较为模式化，大型厂牌发行进一步削弱了其独立属性，与用户关注的实验性、前卫性取向存在一定距离。

items.body: Moments Before ‘Moments Before’ casts Matt Bartram on a sea full of low slung shoe gazed waves and anti static walls of noise. I reviewed his fourth record ‘The Dreaming Invisible’ for this site in 2013. Back then I was wondering how he made such a big sound out of small means. Now I imagine I can ride the vapour trails his aqueous soundscapes formulate. It visualises itself in the nature of new wave St. Vincent. Gorgeous liquid harmony, it’s a place with no excess, primarily settled in glazed surf pop, with elements of Caribou also whisked in the mix. The function of Bartrams voice seems to be the instrumental chewing gum that gets stuck to the mouth of the well engineered synths. It wouldn’t be out of place round here on a set of Slowdive demos for the Eno co-produced Souvlaki album. To this extent, Matt can be connected in kindred spirit to the etherealness of that bands front man, Neil Halstead. He’s complimenting the same auto didactic ideal, being comfortable with controlling everything by the end as much by himself as possible. He’ll possibly always be a drifter, but ‘Moments Before’ stakes it’s claim as one of the best recent albums that I own. Go catch a wave, then come to the shore with this gem. www.driftingfalling.com
items._genre: dream pop / shoegaze / synth pop / surf pop
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续了Bartram的个人项目脉络，整体呈现出水汽弥漫的声响质感。他以自给自足的方式完成大部分制作，人声作为粘合元素嵌入合成器肌理之间，与Slowdive和Eno时代的梦幻流行血脉有精神上的联系。评论将其归入新式梦幻流行的范畴，融合了St. Vincent式的液态和声与Caribou式的电子律动，音色调色板以水面光泽和防静电噪音墙壁为意象。专辑刻意保持精简，没有冗余装饰，所有声音围绕晶莹的合成流行主轴展开。Bartram作为独立创作者，在声场设计和自我掌控上显示出与Neil Halstead相近的自主美学追求。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets
items.label: Hudson
items._cn_summary: Sean Cooney以1819年曼彻斯特圣彼得广场大屠杀（Peterloo）为题材，创作了一组原创歌曲专辑，并以多媒体书籍形式呈现，收录同时代的信件、政治漫画与插图。乐评着重肯定了专辑的历史叙事性——从集会期待到骑兵冲击的恐惧，再到悲恸余波，歌曲以富有画面感的歌词还原了兰开夏工业城镇的历史记忆。Lankashire工业民谣歌手Jennifer Reid担任旁白，Eliza Carthy小提琴与人声、Sam Carter吉他等乐手参与，编制虽小却层次丰富。乐评认为这是一种源于民间传统、承载社会议题的写作，在当下抗议受到打压的时代具有现实意义。整体属于传统民谣叙事范畴，与实验、前卫或电子融合较远，区域文化色彩鲜明但音乐手法偏向传统。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑记录了Dr. John于1999年在德国Loreley露天剧场的演出，由WDR电视台的Rockpalast系列节目录制。演出以新奥尔良风格为核心，融合R&B、funk、布鲁斯等元素，呈现一场Mardi Gras风格的音乐回顾。乐队编制精简但配合紧凑，包含吉他、贝斯和鼓。曲目涵盖新奥尔良经典如'Iko Iko'、Duke Ellington的'I'm Gonna Go Fishin''、Earl King的'Big Chief'等，Dr. John本人的代表作如'Right Place, Wrong Time'和'I Walk on Guilded Splinters'也在其中。'I Walk on Guilded Splinters'展现了Night Tripper时期的巫毒美学，融合丛林音效、滑音哨和迷幻吉他独奏。整张专辑是Dr. John国际声誉巅峰期的现场档案，适合其长期粉丝收藏，对新奥尔良音乐文化的全景式呈现也提供了入门途径。但内容偏向传统根源音乐范畴，与用户关注的实验、前卫、爵士即兴、电子等方向距离较远。

items._cn_summary: 本文讨论的是Public Enemy第四张专辑《Apocalypse 91 The Enemy Strikes Black》的35周年回顾。作者指出该乐队常被视为最具创造力和挑衅性的团体之一，但评论焦点长期停留在第二和第三张专辑上，第四张作品往往被忽视。作者认为这是一张被低估的杰作，其专辑整体编排与节奏设计具有极强的冲击力，延续了乐队标志性的政治表达与密集采样手法。与文章侧重的前两张专辑相比，本文在音乐语言描述上着墨不多，主要从历史地位与文化影响力层面进行再评价，为读者理解这张专辑的定位提供了补充视角。
